```gdscript
extends "res://autoload/BackButtonHandler.gd"
const MODE_SELECT_SCENE := preload("res://scenes/word_game/scrambled/ModeSelect.tscn")
const LESSON_SELECT_SCENE := preload("res://scenes/word_game/scrambled/LessonSelect.tscn")
const GAMEPLAY_SCENE := preload("res://scenes/word_game/scrambled/Gameplay.tscn")
const RESULTS_SCENE := preload("res://scenes/word_game/scrambled/Results.tscn")
const SCENE_WORD_GAME := "res://scenes/word_game/WordGameHub.tscn"
const DEFAULT_TITLE := "بازی املا"
@onready var _header: PanelContainer = $HeaderBar
@onready var _back_button: Button = $HeaderBar/HeaderContent/BackButton
@onready var _title: Label = $HeaderBar/HeaderContent/HeaderTitle
@onready var _host: Control = $ScreenHost
var _screen: Control = null
func _ready() -> void:
	_back_button.pressed.connect(_on_back_pressed)
	_apply_theme()
	Global.on_theme_changed(_on_theme_changed)
	_show_mode_select()
func _on_theme_changed(_mode: int) -> void:
	_apply_theme()
func _apply_theme() -> void:
	var background := $Background as ColorRect
	if background != null:
		background.color = ScrambledTheme.page_tint()
	Global.style_header(_header)
func _on_back_pressed() -> void:
	if _screen != null and _screen.has_method("handle_back"):
		_screen.call("handle_back")
		return
	TransitionManager.change_scene(SCENE_WORD_GAME)
func _on_android_back_pressed() -> void:
	_on_back_pressed()
func _show_mode_select() -> void:
	_swap_to(MODE_SELECT_SCENE)
func _show_lesson_select() -> void:
	_swap_to(LESSON_SELECT_SCENE)
func _show_results() -> void:
	_swap_to(RESULTS_SCENE)
func _start_learning(book: int, lesson: int) -> void:
	if not ScrambledGameManager.start_learning(book, lesson):
		push_warning("ScrambledWords: lesson %d/%d has no playable words" % [book, lesson])
		return
	_swap_to(GAMEPLAY_SCENE)
func _swap_to(scene: PackedScene) -> void:
	var next := scene.instantiate() as Control
	next.set_anchors_preset(Control.PRESET_FULL_RECT)
	next.pivot_offset = _host.size * 0.5
	next.resized.connect(func() -> void: next.pivot_offset = next.size * 0.5)
	next.modulate.a = 0.0
	next.scale = Vector2(0.95, 0.95)
	_host.add_child(next)
	_wire_screen(next)
	var previous := _screen
	_screen = next
	if previous != null:
		var out := create_tween()
		out.tween_property(previous, "modulate:a", 0.0, 0.16).set_trans(Tween.TRANS_QUAD).set_ease(Tween.EASE_IN)
		out.tween_callback(previous.queue_free)
	var tw := create_tween()
	tw.tween_property(next, "modulate:a", 1.0, 0.26).set_trans(Tween.TRANS_QUAD).set_ease(Tween.EASE_OUT)
	tw.parallel().tween_property(next, "scale", Vector2.ONE, 0.36).set_trans(Tween.TRANS_BACK).set_ease(Tween.EASE_OUT)
	_update_title()
func _wire_screen(screen: Control) -> void:
	if screen.has_signal("learning_requested"):
		screen.connect("learning_requested", _show_lesson_select)
	if screen.has_signal("exit_requested"):
		screen.connect("exit_requested", _leave_game)
	if screen.has_signal("lesson_chosen"):
		screen.connect("lesson_chosen", _start_learning)
	if screen.has_signal("back_requested"):
		screen.connect("back_requested", _show_mode_select)
	if screen.has_signal("quit_requested"):
		screen.connect("quit_requested", _leave_to_modes)
	if screen.has_signal("session_finished"):
		screen.connect("session_finished", _show_results)
	if screen.has_signal("home_requested"):
		screen.connect("home_requested", _show_mode_select)
	if screen.has_signal("replay_requested"):
		screen.connect("replay_requested", _replay)
func _leave_game() -> void:
	TransitionManager.change_scene(SCENE_WORD_GAME)
func _leave_to_modes() -> void:
	if ScrambledGameManager.mode == ScrambledGameManager.Mode.LEARNING:
		_show_lesson_select()
	else:
		_show_mode_select()
func _replay() -> void:
	if ScrambledGameManager.mode == ScrambledGameManager.Mode.COMPETITION:
		_show_mode_select()
	else:
		_start_learning(ScrambledGameManager.book, ScrambledGameManager.lesson)
func _update_title() -> void:
	if _screen != null and _screen.has_method("screen_title"):
		_title.text = str(_screen.call("screen_title"))
		return
	_title.text = DEFAULT_TITLE
```

```gdscript
class_name ScrambledTile
extends Control
## ============================================================
##  SCRAMBLED TILE — one draggable letter of «بازی املا».
##
##  WHY IT DRAWS ITSELF instead of being a Panel + Label: the app-wide theme
##  walk (ThemeService) restyles every Panel/PanelContainer/Label it finds.
##  Running over a board mid-puzzle it would erase the candy colours, the
##  solved green and the amber nudge, and repaint every letter in the theme
##  colour. A self-drawing Control is invisible to that walk, so a board
##  keeps its state and survives a live theme toggle. WordleTile solved the
##  same problem the same way.
##
##  DRAG & DROP — the native Control protocol, per the project's UI rules:
##    _get_drag_data()  hands the Viewport a payload AND the preview the
##                      player carries (TilePreview),
##    _can_drop_data()  lets the pointer be followed across the row,
##    _drop_data()      reports where the letter was let go.
##
##  WHY A TILE ACCEPTS A DROP IT DOES NOT PLACE ITSELF: the Viewport's drop
##  search stops at the first MOUSE_FILTER_STOP control that refuses a drop
##  and will not walk on to the board underneath. A tile returning false
##  would make the row itself undroppable. Accepting costs nothing, and the
##  placement stays the board's business — this node only reports the finger
##  through signals and never touches the row (see the project's UI rules).
## ============================================================

## The finger picked a letter up: the board opens a slot for it.
signal drag_started(tile: ScrambledTile)
## The carried letter is over `pointer_canvas`: the board previews the slot.
signal drag_hovered(tile: ScrambledTile, pointer_canvas: Vector2)
## The letter was let go over `pointer_canvas`: the board decides where.
signal drop_requested(tile: ScrambledTile, pointer_canvas: Vector2)
## The drag ended without a drop (finger off the row, gesture cancelled).
## The board puts the letter back where it came from.
signal drag_cancelled(tile: ScrambledTile)

enum State { IDLE, DRAGGING, SOLVED, LOCKED }

## Every payload this scene's drags carry is tagged, so a drag started on
## another screen is rejected outright instead of half-read.
const PAYLOAD_KIND := "scrambled_tile"
const PREVIEW_SCENE := preload("res://scenes/word_game/scrambled/ui/TilePreview.tscn")

## The look is copied from the reference tiles the game is styled after:
## a flat candy face, a darker extruded bottom edge (a chunky 3D block), a
## dark outline around the whole block and one big, very round white letter.
const CORNER_RATIO := 0.34
const OUTLINE_RATIO := 0.085
const SIDE_RATIO := 0.16          # extruded bottom edge, as a fraction of size
const LETTER_RATIO := 0.62
const MIN_LETTER_SIZE := 18
## Desktop hover feedback (touch never sees it).
const HOVER_SCALE := 1.05
## How solid a tile stays while it is carried. The copy in the player's hand
## (the drag preview) is the live one; this is the ghost it left behind, and
## dimming it is what makes the pulsing empty slot read as "the letter is
## in flight".
const DRAG_GHOST_ALPHA := 0.28
## Fade back up once the finger lets go — on a drop and a cancellation alike.
const DRAG_FADE_TIME := 0.18

var letter := ""
var color_index := 0
var slot_id := 0

var state: State = State.IDLE:
	set(value):
		state = value
		_apply_drag_tint()
		_refresh()

## 0..1 cartoon elevation, kept for the board's settle tween.
var lift := 0.0:
	set(value):
		lift = clampf(value, 0.0, 1.0)
		_refresh()

## 0..1 amber pulse of the "not quite right yet" nudge.
var nudge := 0.0:
	set(value):
		nudge = clampf(value, 0.0, 1.0)
		_refresh()

var _hovered := false
var _style := StyleBoxFlat.new()
## Set when the board actually takes the letter. NOTIFICATION_DRAG_END fires
## for a completed drop too, and must not report it as a cancellation.
var _drop_accepted := false


func _ready() -> void:
	# STOP: the tile has to catch the press that starts a drag, and has to
	# stay reachable as a drop target (see the class docs).
	mouse_filter = Control.MOUSE_FILTER_STOP
	focus_mode = Control.FOCUS_NONE
	resized.connect(_on_resized)
	mouse_entered.connect(_on_mouse_entered)
	mouse_exited.connect(_on_mouse_exited)
	_refresh()


func _on_resized() -> void:
	pivot_offset = size * 0.5
	_refresh()


## Sizes the tile. Called by the board for every tile of the row.
func set_tile_size(px: float) -> void:
	var wanted := Vector2(maxf(px, 32.0), maxf(px, 32.0))
	if size == wanted:
		return
	size = wanted
	pivot_offset = size * 0.5
	_refresh()


## Paints the tile as a solved (green) letter, or takes the green away again.
func set_solved(value: bool) -> void:
	state = State.SOLVED if value else State.IDLE


func is_solved() -> bool:
	return state == State.SOLVED


## A locked tile takes no input: used while the row settles and when the word
## is finished. A tile the finger is still carrying is never locked — the
## gesture owns it until it is let go.
func set_locked(value: bool) -> void:
	if value:
		if state == State.DRAGGING:
			return
		state = State.LOCKED
	elif state == State.LOCKED:
		state = State.IDLE


## Pops the tile: the win wave, and the moment a word is dealt.
func play_pop(delay: float = 0.0, strength: float = 1.16) -> void:
	pivot_offset = size * 0.5
	var tw := create_tween()
	tw.tween_interval(maxf(delay, 0.0))
	tw.tween_property(self, "scale", Vector2(strength, strength), 0.12) \
		.set_trans(Tween.TRANS_QUAD).set_ease(Tween.EASE_OUT)
	tw.tween_property(self, "scale", Vector2.ONE, 0.18) \
		.set_trans(Tween.TRANS_BACK).set_ease(Tween.EASE_OUT)


## A short, friendly wobble with an amber flash: "that letter sits wrong",
## never "you failed" — and it never reveals the answer.
func play_nudge() -> void:
	var tw := create_tween()
	tw.tween_property(self, "nudge", 1.0, 0.14).set_trans(Tween.TRANS_SINE).set_ease(Tween.EASE_OUT)
	tw.tween_property(self, "nudge", 0.0, 0.42).set_trans(Tween.TRANS_SINE).set_ease(Tween.EASE_IN_OUT)
	var wobble := create_tween()
	wobble.tween_property(self, "rotation", 0.05, 0.08).set_trans(Tween.TRANS_SINE).set_ease(Tween.EASE_OUT)
	wobble.tween_property(self, "rotation", -0.05, 0.12).set_trans(Tween.TRANS_SINE).set_ease(Tween.EASE_IN_OUT)
	wobble.tween_property(self, "rotation", 0.0, 0.10).set_trans(Tween.TRANS_SINE).set_ease(Tween.EASE_IN_OUT)


## Resizes a pointer position into the shared canvas space: the positions the
## drag protocol hands us are local to whichever node received the event, and
## the tile may be scaled or mid-tween at that moment.
func global_pointer(local: Vector2) -> Vector2:
	return get_global_transform() * local


## ------------------------------------------------- drag & drop (rule 2) --
## The Viewport calls this once the finger has travelled far enough with the
## button down. Returning a non-empty payload is what starts a native drag;
## returning null leaves the tile inert (the solved and locked states).
func _get_drag_data(at_position: Vector2) -> Variant:
	if state == State.LOCKED or state == State.SOLVED:
		return null
	_drop_accepted = false
	_attach_preview()
	state = State.DRAGGING
	drag_started.emit(self)
	# Report the very first position too, so the row opens up under the letter
	# immediately instead of waiting for the first motion event.
	drag_hovered.emit(self, global_pointer(at_position))
	return {
		"kind": PAYLOAD_KIND,
		"tile": self,
		"slot_id": slot_id,
		"letter": letter,
	}


## Rule 2's visual preview: the player must always see what they hold. Handing
## one over is only legal while the Viewport is really running a drag, and the
## engine refuses it otherwise — so the check also keeps a direct call (a unit
## test driving this method) from tripping that guard.
func _attach_preview() -> void:
	var viewport := get_viewport()
	if viewport == null or not viewport.gui_is_dragging():
		return
	var preview := PREVIEW_SCENE.instantiate() as TilePreview
	if preview == null:
		return
	preview.configure(letter, color_index, size.x)
	set_drag_preview(preview)


## A tile takes a carried letter so the row stays droppable (see the class
## docs). It only relays the position; the board does the placing.
##
## The hover is reported even when the finger is back over the carried letter's
## own slot: the board has to hear about that position like any other, or its
## open slot would stay wherever the finger last left it.
func _can_drop_data(at_position: Vector2, data: Variant) -> bool:
	var carried := payload_tile(data)
	if carried == null:
		return false
	carried.report_hover(global_pointer(at_position))
	return true


func _drop_data(at_position: Vector2, data: Variant) -> void:
	var carried := payload_tile(data)
	if carried == null:
		return
	carried.report_drop(global_pointer(at_position))


## The tile a payload belongs to, or null when the payload is not one of ours.
static func payload_tile(data: Variant) -> ScrambledTile:
	if typeof(data) != TYPE_DICTIONARY:
		return null
	var payload := data as Dictionary
	if str(payload.get("kind", "")) != PAYLOAD_KIND:
		return null
	return payload.get("tile") as ScrambledTile


## Called by the drop target under the finger. Kept as a method rather than a
## flag written from outside, so the drag state stays this node's own.
func report_hover(pointer_canvas: Vector2) -> void:
	if state == State.DRAGGING:
		drag_hovered.emit(self, pointer_canvas)


func report_drop(pointer_canvas: Vector2) -> void:
	if state != State.DRAGGING:
		return
	_drop_accepted = true
	drop_requested.emit(self, pointer_canvas)


## Called by the board once it has taken the letter: the drag is consumed, so
## the tile stops being a ghost and becomes an ordinary member of the row.
func accept_drop() -> void:
	_drop_accepted = true
	state = State.IDLE


## The drag is over either way. A drop has already been handed to the board;
## anything else is a cancellation and the letter goes back to its slot.
func _notification(what: int) -> void:
	if what != NOTIFICATION_DRAG_END:
		return
	var accepted := _drop_accepted
	_drop_accepted = false
	if state != State.DRAGGING:
		return
	state = State.IDLE
	if not accepted:
		drag_cancelled.emit(self)


func _on_mouse_entered() -> void:
	_hovered = true
	if state != State.IDLE:
		return
	var tw := create_tween()
	tw.tween_property(self, "scale", Vector2(HOVER_SCALE, HOVER_SCALE), 0.14) \
		.set_trans(Tween.TRANS_QUAD).set_ease(Tween.EASE_OUT)


func _on_mouse_exited() -> void:
	_hovered = false
	if state != State.IDLE:
		return
	var tw := create_tween()
	tw.tween_property(self, "scale", Vector2.ONE, 0.14) \
		.set_trans(Tween.TRANS_QUAD).set_ease(Tween.EASE_OUT)


## Dims the tile while the finger carries it and fades it back the moment it
## is let go — on a drop, a cancellation or a lock alike, so the ghost can
## never outlive the gesture. Every other writer of this alpha (the deal
## animation) only ever runs while the tile is IDLE, so nothing fights
## over it.
func _apply_drag_tint() -> void:
	var target := DRAG_GHOST_ALPHA if state == State.DRAGGING else 1.0
	if is_equal_approx(modulate.a, target):
		return
	if state == State.DRAGGING or not is_inside_tree():
		# Entering the drag must be instant — a fade-in would look like lag.
		modulate.a = target
		return
	var tw := create_tween()
	tw.tween_property(self, "modulate:a", target, DRAG_FADE_TIME) \
		.set_trans(Tween.TRANS_QUAD).set_ease(Tween.EASE_OUT)


## --------------------------------------------------------------- drawing --
func _body_color() -> Color:
	if state == State.SOLVED:
		return ScrambledTheme.SOLVED_COLOR
	var base := ScrambledTheme.tile_color(color_index)
	if nudge > 0.0:
		return base.lerp(ScrambledTheme.NUDGE_COLOR, nudge * 0.5)
	return base


## The single source of truth for the tile's look.
func _refresh() -> void:
	if size.x <= 0.0:
		return
	var radius := int(maxf(8.0, size.x * CORNER_RATIO))
	# The dark outline is the back-most block; the candy face and its extruded
	# edge are drawn on top of it, inset by the outline's thickness.
	_style.set_corner_radius_all(radius)
	_style.set_border_width_all(0)
	_style.bg_color = ScrambledTheme.TILE_OUTLINE
	# Cartoon elevation while lifted: a soft drop shadow behind the whole
	# block, on top of the solid extruded edge it always has.
	_style.shadow_color = Color(0.10, 0.06, 0.20, 0.18 + 0.26 * lift)
	_style.shadow_size = int(round(4.0 + 16.0 * lift))
	_style.shadow_offset = Vector2(0.0, 6.0 + 10.0 * lift)
	queue_redraw()


func _draw() -> void:
	if size.x <= 0.0 or size.y <= 0.0:
		return
	var body := _body_color()
	var radius := maxf(8.0, size.x * CORNER_RATIO)
	var outline := maxf(2.0, size.x * OUTLINE_RATIO)
	var side := maxf(4.0, size.x * SIDE_RATIO)
	var inner := size - Vector2(outline * 2.0, outline * 2.0)
	if inner.x <= 0.0 or inner.y - side <= 0.0:
		return

	# 1. The dark outline: a solid block behind everything.
	draw_style_box(_style, Rect2(Vector2.ZERO, size))
	# 2. The extruded bottom edge: a darker slab of the same colour, drawn
	#    over the outline and covered by the face, so only its bottom lip
	#    shows — that lip is what makes the tile a chunky 3D block.
	draw_style_box(_slab_style(ScrambledTheme.tile_side(body), radius),
		Rect2(Vector2(outline, outline), inner))
	# 3. The face: the flat candy colour, lifted by the extrusion.
	draw_style_box(_slab_style(body, radius),
		Rect2(Vector2(outline, outline), Vector2(inner.x, inner.y - side)))
	# 4. A subtle gloss across the top of the face.
	var gloss_height := maxf(4.0, (inner.y - side) * 0.30)
	draw_style_box(_slab_style(Color(1, 1, 1, 0.20), int(radius * 0.7)),
		Rect2(Vector2(outline + radius * 0.28, outline + radius * 0.20),
			Vector2(inner.x - radius * 0.56, gloss_height)))

	if letter.is_empty():
		return
	var font := MenuStyle.nunito()
	if font == null:
		font = get_theme_default_font()
	if font == null:
		return
	# One big, very round white letter, centred on the face (slightly above
	# the middle so the extrusion does not make it read as sitting low).
	var letter_size := int(maxf(float(MIN_LETTER_SIZE), size.x * LETTER_RATIO))
	var face_center := outline + (inner.y - side) * 0.5
	var ascent := font.get_ascent(letter_size)
	var descent := font.get_descent(letter_size)
	var baseline := face_center + (ascent - descent) * 0.5
	draw_string(font, Vector2(0.0, baseline), letter, HORIZONTAL_ALIGNMENT_CENTER,
		size.x, letter_size, ScrambledTheme.tile_letter(body))


func _slab_style(color: Color, radius: float) -> StyleBoxFlat:
	var style := StyleBoxFlat.new()
	style.set_corner_radius_all(int(radius))
	style.set_border_width_all(0)
	style.bg_color = color
	return style
```

```gdscript
class_name ScrambledTileBoard
extends Control
## ============================================================
##  SCRAMBLED TILE BOARD — the row of letters the player rearranges.
##
##  This is where the drag-and-drop lives. The gesture itself is the native
##  Control protocol — a tile hands the Viewport its payload and the carried
##  copy the player holds (see tile.gd) — while this node is the one that
##  DECIDES. It is deliberate about how that feels on a phone:
##    * the slot under the carried letter opens up the instant the pickup is
##      reported, and the neighbours slide out of the way (TRANS_BACK, so
##      they settle with a little bounce) around a pulsing outline,
##    * the drop snaps with TRANS_BACK/EASE_OUT, and a wrong arrangement is
##      never punished — if the word is one or two letters away the misplaced
##      tiles pulse amber, which nudges without revealing the answer,
##    * a drag that ends anywhere else puts the letter back, so a slipped
##      finger can never lose a letter off the row.
##
##  The board owns every position: tiles only REPORT the finger, and they do
##  that through signals, never by reaching back into this node. The child
##  order is re-synced after each settle so the next carried letter comes to
##  the front, and the layout is recomputed from the board's own size, so a
##  three letter word and a twelve letter word both fit and stay square.
## ============================================================

signal arrangement_settled(solved: bool)
signal tile_grabbed(tile: ScrambledTile)

const TILE_SCENE := preload("res://scenes/word_game/scrambled/Tile.tscn")

const MAX_TILE_SIZE := 200.0
const MIN_TILE_SIZE := 40.0
const MIN_GAP := 8.0
const MAX_GAP := 26.0
## The row sits a little below the centre, keeping the thumb off the letters.
const ROW_TOP_BIAS := 26.0
## How long a neighbour takes to slide out of the way when a slot opens up.
const SHIFT_TIME := 0.20
const SETTLE_TIME := 0.24
const DEAL_STAGGER := 0.06
const DEAL_TIME := 0.30

var _controller: ScrambledWordController = null
## slot_id -> ScrambledTile. A slot id is a tile's identity, not its place.
var _tiles: Array = []
## Slot ids left to right, as committed (what the word is judged against).
var _order: Array = []
## The committed order with the carried tile previewed in its slot.
var _display_order: Array = []
var _held: ScrambledTile = null
var _preview_index := -1
var _ghost_index := -1
var _solved := false
var _locked := false
var _tile_size := 120.0
var _gap := 18.0
var _row_y := 0.0
var _settle_waiter: Tween = null
var _ghost_seeker: Tween = null
## True while the row is flying in. A layout change during the deal restarts it
## whole, because the deal starts from alpha 0: cancelling it would leave the
## row invisible.
var _dealing := false
## Ends the deal and declares the row at rest.
var _deal_waiter: Tween = null
var _track_style := StyleBoxFlat.new()
var _ghost_style := StyleBoxFlat.new()
## "instance_property" -> the tween currently driving it, so a new move can
## replace an old one instead of fighting it.
var _moves: Dictionary = {}

## 0..1 pulse of the empty slot outline (looping while a tile is carried).
var _ghost_pulse := 0.0:
	set(value):
		_ghost_pulse = clampf(value, 0.0, 1.0)
		_update_ghost_style()
## ------------------------------------------------------------- building --
func _ready() -> void:
	mouse_filter = Control.MOUSE_FILTER_PASS
	resized.connect(_on_resized)
	_refresh_styles()


## Deals a word: one tile per letter, in the controller's scrambled order.
func build(p_controller: ScrambledWordController, animate := true) -> void:
	clear()
	_controller = p_controller
	if _controller == null:
		return
	for i in _controller.letters.size():
		var tile := TILE_SCENE.instantiate() as ScrambledTile
		tile.letter = str(_controller.letters[i])
		tile.color_index = i
		tile.slot_id = i
		add_child(tile)
		# The drag protocol belongs to the tile (see tile.gd); the board only
		# listens, and decides where the letter lands.
		tile.drag_started.connect(_on_tile_drag_started)
		tile.drag_hovered.connect(_on_tile_drag_hovered)
		tile.drop_requested.connect(_on_tile_drop_requested)
		tile.drag_cancelled.connect(_on_tile_drag_cancelled)
		_tiles.append(tile)
		_order.append(i)
	_display_order = _order.duplicate()
	# The first word of a session is built in the same frame the screen lays
	# out, so the board may not know its size yet. Dealing with a guessed
	# geometry would drop the letters in the wrong place, so wait one frame
	# for the real layout first.
	if size.y < 40.0:
		await get_tree().process_frame
		if not is_inside_tree() or _controller != p_controller:
			return
	_recompute_layout()
	if animate:
		_deal_animation()
	else:
		for tile in _tiles:
			tile.play_pop(0.0, 1.0)


func clear() -> void:
	_kill_tweens()
	_held = null
	_preview_index = -1
	_ghost_index = -1
	_solved = false
	_locked = false
	for tile in _tiles:
		if is_instance_valid(tile):
			tile.queue_free()
	_tiles = []
	_order = []
	_display_order = []
	_controller = null
	queue_redraw()


## Fades the row in: each tile flies up from below with a small pop, which
## reads as the letters being "dealt" rather than appearing. The tweens go
## through _tween(), so a second call (a layout change mid-deal) replaces them
## instead of stacking, and grabbing a letter mid-deal takes it over cleanly.
func _deal_animation() -> void:
	_dealing = true
	for i in _tiles.size():
		var tile := _tiles[i] as ScrambledTile
		var slot := _slot_position(i)
		var delay := DEAL_STAGGER * float(i)
		tile.position = slot + Vector2(0.0, 90.0)
		tile.modulate.a = 0.0
		tile.scale = Vector2(0.75, 0.75)
		_tween(tile, "position", slot, DEAL_TIME, Tween.TRANS_BACK, Tween.EASE_OUT, delay)
		_tween(tile, "scale", Vector2.ONE, DEAL_TIME, Tween.TRANS_BACK, Tween.EASE_OUT, delay)
		_tween(tile, "modulate:a", 1.0, DEAL_TIME * 0.7, Tween.TRANS_QUAD, Tween.EASE_OUT, delay)
	# The row counts as settled only once the last tile has landed: whatever the
	# layout does underneath it, the deal ends with a fully visible row.
	if _deal_waiter != null and _deal_waiter.is_valid():
		_deal_waiter.kill()
	var total := DEAL_TIME + DEAL_STAGGER * float(maxi(_tiles.size() - 1, 0))
	_deal_waiter = create_tween()
	_deal_waiter.tween_interval(total + 0.05)
	_deal_waiter.tween_callback(_finish_deal)


func _finish_deal() -> void:
	_deal_waiter = null
	_dealing = false
	# Safety net: the deal is the only move that fades a tile, so a tile that
	# reached the end of it is visible, exactly where it was aimed.
	for tile in _tiles:
		if is_instance_valid(tile):
			(tile as ScrambledTile).modulate.a = 1.0
	queue_redraw()


## ------------------------------------------------------------- geometry --
func _on_resized() -> void:
	_recompute_layout()


func _recompute_layout() -> void:
	if _order.is_empty():
		return
	var width := size.x if size.x > 60.0 else 980.0
	var gap := clampf(width * 0.013, MIN_GAP, MAX_GAP)
	var count := _order.size()
	var tile_px := (width - gap * float(count - 1)) / float(count)
	_tile_size = clampf(tile_px, MIN_TILE_SIZE, MAX_TILE_SIZE)
	_gap = gap
	_row_y = (size.y - _tile_size) * 0.5 + ROW_TOP_BIAS
	for i in count:
		var tile := _tiles[_order[i]] as ScrambledTile
		tile.set_tile_size(_tile_size)
	_refresh_styles()
	queue_redraw()
	# A layout change moves the slots, so every move in flight is re-issued
	# against the new ones instead of being left to run to a stale target —
	# and nothing is simply killed: the deal fades in from alpha 0, so an
	# abandoned deal would leave the row invisible.
	if _dealing and _held == null:
		_deal_animation()
		return
	if _held != null:
		# The finger owns the carried tile; only the tiles making room for it
		# are re-slotted.
		_set_preview(_preview_index)
		return
	var was_settling := _settle_waiter != null and _settle_waiter.is_valid()
	for i in count:
		var tile := _tiles[_order[i]] as ScrambledTile
		tile.modulate.a = 1.0
		_tween(tile, "position", _slot_position(i), SHIFT_TIME,
			Tween.TRANS_QUAD, Tween.EASE_OUT)
	if was_settling:
		_schedule_settle()


## Total width of the row, and the x of its left edge (the row is centred).
func _row_width() -> float:
	var count := _order.size()
	return _tile_size * float(count) + _gap * float(maxi(count - 1, 0))


func _origin_x() -> float:
	return (size.x - _row_width()) * 0.5


func _slot_position(index: int) -> Vector2:
	return Vector2(_origin_x() + float(index) * (_tile_size + _gap), _row_y)


## The slot a carried letter is hovering over, from the pointer's x. The
## pointer stands in for the letter's centre: the drag preview is centred on
## the finger, so the two agree.
func _index_for_center(center_x: float) -> int:
	var step := _tile_size + _gap
	var raw := (center_x - _origin_x() - _tile_size * 0.5) / step
	return clampi(int(round(raw)), 0, maxi(_order.size() - 1, 0))


## Pointer positions arrive in the shared canvas space; the board thinks and
## works in its own local space (Control has no to_local()).
func _to_board(global_point: Vector2) -> Vector2:
	return get_global_transform().affine_inverse() * global_point


## -------------------------------------------------------- drop target --
## The board accepts a carried letter in its own right, so a drop that lands
## between two slots — or on the track's padding — still goes to the nearest
## one instead of bouncing home. At any other time the board stays inert,
## which is what lets the Viewport keep walking up to its parent.
##
## It reports the hover too: when no letter is under the finger the board is
## the control that answers, and the open slot still has to follow.
func _can_drop_data(at_position: Vector2, data: Variant) -> bool:
	var carried := ScrambledTile.payload_tile(data)
	if carried == null or _held != carried:
		return false
	_on_tile_drag_hovered(carried, get_global_transform() * at_position)
	return true


func _drop_data(at_position: Vector2, data: Variant) -> void:
	var carried := ScrambledTile.payload_tile(data)
	if carried == null or _held != carried:
		return
	# at_position is handed over in this board's own space already.
	_commit_drop(carried, _index_for_center(at_position.x))


## ----------------------------------------------------------- drag & drop --
## The board listens to the tiles' drag protocol (tile.gd) and owns every
## decision: which slot opens up while a letter is carried, and where it lands
## when it is let go. A tile never moves itself or its neighbours.
func _on_tile_drag_started(tile: ScrambledTile) -> void:
	if _locked or _solved or _held != null:
		return
	# A settle still in flight is committed right away: picking a letter up
	# must never have to wait for an animation.
	_finish_settle_now()
	# The deal stops being a unit the moment a letter is picked up out of it:
	# the tiles still flying finish their own moves, but a layout change from
	# here on must not restart the whole row — that would yank the slot out
	# from under the letter the player is holding.
	_dealing = false
	_held = tile
	_preview_index = _order.find(tile.slot_id)
	_display_order = _order.duplicate()
	_ghost_index = _preview_index
	tile.move_to_front()
	_start_ghost_seeker()
	queue_redraw()
	tile_grabbed.emit(tile)


## Follows the finger: the slot under the carried letter opens up and the
## neighbours slide out of the way to make room for it.
func _on_tile_drag_hovered(tile: ScrambledTile, pointer_canvas: Vector2) -> void:
	if _held != tile:
		return
	var index := _index_for_center(_to_board(pointer_canvas).x)
	if index != _preview_index:
		_set_preview(index)


## Opens the slot at `index`: every other tile slides to where it will sit
## once the carried tile is dropped there.
func _set_preview(index: int) -> void:
	_preview_index = index
	_ghost_index = index
	_display_order = _order.duplicate()
	_display_order.erase(_held.slot_id)
	_display_order.insert(index, _held.slot_id)
	for i in _display_order.size():
		var tile := _tiles[_display_order[i]] as ScrambledTile
		if tile == _held:
			continue
		_tween(tile, "position", _slot_position(i), SHIFT_TIME, Tween.TRANS_BACK, Tween.EASE_OUT)
	queue_redraw()


func _on_tile_drop_requested(tile: ScrambledTile, pointer_canvas: Vector2) -> void:
	if _held != tile:
		return
	_commit_drop(tile, _index_for_center(_to_board(pointer_canvas).x))


## The finger never let go over the row (or the gesture was cancelled): the
## letters simply settle back into the order they were carried out of, so a
## slipped finger can never lose a letter.
func _on_tile_drag_cancelled(tile: ScrambledTile) -> void:
	if _held != tile:
		return
	_held = null
	_ghost_index = -1
	_preview_index = -1
	_stop_ghost_seeker()
	_display_order = _order.duplicate()
	_settle_row(tile)


## The letter is taken: the order previewed while it was carried becomes the
## real one, and the row settles around it.
func _commit_drop(tile: ScrambledTile, index: int) -> void:
	_set_preview(index)
	tile.accept_drop()
	_held = null
	_ghost_index = -1
	_stop_ghost_seeker()
	_order = _display_order.duplicate()
	_settle_row(tile)


## Commits the row: every letter slides into its slot with the settle pop, and
## the arrangement is judged once they have all landed. Shared by a drop and a
## cancelled drag, so both end exactly the same way.
func _settle_row(source: ScrambledTile) -> void:
	for i in _order.size():
		var tile := _tiles[_order[i]] as ScrambledTile
		tile.set_locked(true)
		_tween(tile, "position", _slot_position(i), SETTLE_TIME, Tween.TRANS_BACK, Tween.EASE_OUT)
	# The carried letter flies home rather than snapping: the preview vanishes
	# the instant the finger lifts, so this is what makes the drop read as the
	# letter landing in its new slot.
	_tween(source, "scale", Vector2.ONE, SETTLE_TIME, Tween.TRANS_BACK, Tween.EASE_OUT)
	_tween(source, "lift", 0.0, SETTLE_TIME, Tween.TRANS_QUAD, Tween.EASE_OUT)
	_schedule_settle()


func _schedule_settle() -> void:
	if _settle_waiter != null and _settle_waiter.is_valid():
		_settle_waiter.kill()
	_settle_waiter = create_tween()
	_settle_waiter.tween_interval(SETTLE_TIME + 0.05)
	_settle_waiter.tween_callback(_finish_settle)


## Called by a new grab: everything still moving is snapped home first.
func _finish_settle_now() -> void:
	if _settle_waiter != null and _settle_waiter.is_valid():
		_settle_waiter.kill()
	_settle_waiter = null
	_finish_settle()


func _finish_settle() -> void:
	_settle_waiter = null
	if _tiles.is_empty():
		return
	var solved := is_solved()
	if solved:
		_solved = true
	# Positions are pinned exactly and the child order goes back to the board
	# order: the carried tile was drawn on top (move_to_front) and that must
	# not outlive the move, or the next lifted letter would hide behind it.
	for i in _order.size():
		var tile := _tiles[_order[i]] as ScrambledTile
		tile.position = _slot_position(i)
		tile.rotation = 0.0
		move_child(tile, i)
		if not solved:
			tile.set_locked(false)
	queue_redraw()
	arrangement_settled.emit(solved)


## -------------------------------------------------------------- readings --
## The letters as they currently stand, left to right.
func tiles_letters() -> Array:
	var out: Array = []
	for slot in _order:
		out.append((_tiles[slot] as ScrambledTile).letter)
	return out


func current_text() -> String:
	return ScrambledWordController.letters_to_text(tiles_letters())


func is_solved() -> bool:
	if _controller == null:
		return false
	return _controller.is_solved(tiles_letters())


func is_busy() -> bool:
	return _held != null


func tile_count() -> int:
	return _order.size()


## Freezes the board: while a word is being dealt, while it is solved, and for
## the beat before the next word arrives.
func set_board_locked(value: bool) -> void:
	_locked = value
	for tile in _tiles:
		(tile as ScrambledTile).set_locked(value or _solved)
## ------------------------------------------------------------ flourishes --
## The win: a green wave that runs left to right, then every tile stays green.
func play_solved_flourish() -> void:
	_solved = true
	for i in _order.size():
		var tile := _tiles[_order[i]] as ScrambledTile
		tile.play_pop(0.07 * float(i), 1.22)
		var tw := create_tween()
		tw.tween_interval(0.10 + 0.07 * float(i))
		tw.tween_callback(func() -> void: tile.set_solved(true))
	queue_redraw()


## Reveals a letter at the given index.
func reveal_letter_at(index: int) -> void:
	if index < 0 or index >= _tiles.size():
		return
	var tile := _tiles[_order[index]] as ScrambledTile
	if tile != null:
		# Optionally animate the reveal
		tile.play_pop(0.0, 1.1)
		# Perhaps lock it too?
		tile.set_locked(true)


## Ambers the tiles that sit in the wrong place. Only ever used when the word
## is one or two letters away, so it nudges without spoiling the answer.
func play_near_miss_nudge() -> void:
	if _controller == null:
		return
	for index in _controller.misplaced(tiles_letters()):
		var tile := _tiles[_order[index]] as ScrambledTile
		if tile != null:
			tile.play_nudge()


## --------------------------------------------------------------- drawing --
func _update_ghost_style() -> void:
	_ghost_style.bg_color = ScrambledTheme.ghost_color(_ghost_pulse)
	_ghost_style.border_color = ScrambledTheme.ghost_border_color(_ghost_pulse)
	queue_redraw()


func _refresh_styles() -> void:
	_track_style.bg_color = ScrambledTheme.track_color()
	_track_style.set_corner_radius_all(int(_tile_size * 0.30) + 10)
	_track_style.set_border_width_all(0)
	_ghost_style.set_corner_radius_all(int(_tile_size * 0.26))
	_ghost_style.set_border_width_all(4)
	_update_ghost_style()


## The board paints what lives between the tiles: the soft track that shows
## where the row is, and the pulsing slot the carried tile would drop into.
func _draw() -> void:
	if _order.is_empty():
		return
	var pad := maxf(18.0, _tile_size * 0.16)
	draw_style_box(_track_style, Rect2(
		Vector2(_origin_x() - pad, _row_y - pad * 0.6),
		Vector2(_row_width() + pad * 2.0, _tile_size + pad * 1.2)))
	if _ghost_index >= 0 and _held != null:
		draw_style_box(_ghost_style, Rect2(_slot_position(_ghost_index),
			Vector2(_tile_size, _tile_size)))


## ---------------------------------------------------------- tween helpers --
## One tween per tile and property: a fresh move (a new preview slot, a grab
## during the settle) replaces the old one instead of fighting it.
func _tween(target: Object, property: String, value: Variant, time: float,
		trans: Tween.TransitionType, ease_type: Tween.EaseType, delay := 0.0) -> void:
	var key := "%d_%s" % [target.get_instance_id(), property]
	var previous: Tween = _moves.get(key)
	if previous != null and previous.is_valid():
		previous.kill()
	var tw := create_tween()
	var tweener := tw.tween_property(target, property, value, time)
	tweener.set_trans(trans).set_ease(ease_type)
	if delay > 0.0:
		tweener.set_delay(delay)
	_moves[key] = tw


func _start_ghost_seeker() -> void:
	_stop_ghost_seeker()
	_ghost_seeker = create_tween().set_loops()
	_ghost_seeker.tween_property(self, "_ghost_pulse", 1.0, 0.55) \
		.set_trans(Tween.TRANS_SINE).set_ease(Tween.EASE_IN_OUT)
	_ghost_seeker.tween_property(self, "_ghost_pulse", 0.0, 0.55) \
		.set_trans(Tween.TRANS_SINE).set_ease(Tween.EASE_IN_OUT)


func _stop_ghost_seeker() -> void:
	if _ghost_seeker != null and _ghost_seeker.is_valid():
		_ghost_seeker.kill()
	_ghost_seeker = null
	_ghost_pulse = 0.0


func _kill_tweens() -> void:
	if _settle_waiter != null and _settle_waiter.is_valid():
		_settle_waiter.kill()
	_settle_waiter = null
	if _deal_waiter != null and _deal_waiter.is_valid():
		_deal_waiter.kill()
	_deal_waiter = null
	_dealing = false
	_stop_ghost_seeker()
	for tween in _moves.values():
		if tween != null and (tween as Tween).is_valid():
			(tween as Tween).kill()
	_moves = {}
```

## File: `res://scenes/word_game/scrambled/ui/confetti_burst.gd`

```gdscript
class_name ScrambledConfettiBurst
extends CPUParticles2D
## ============================================================
##  CONFETTI BURST — the celebration thrown when a word is spelled.
##
##  Every numeric setting of the fountain lives in the scene, so the shape of
##  the burst can be tuned without touching code. What CANNOT live in a scene
##  is built here: the particle is a white square drawn at runtime (no image
##  asset needed) and the two colour ramps are read from the palette, so a
##  burst thrown after a live theme toggle still matches the tiles it is
##  celebrating.
## ============================================================

const DOT_PX := 10

var _dot: Texture2D = null


func _ready() -> void:
	_dot = _make_dot()
	texture = _dot
	apply_theme()


## Fires one burst centred on `at`, in this node's parent space.
func burst(at: Vector2) -> void:
	position = at
	emitting = true


func apply_theme() -> void:
	color_initial_ramp = _tile_ramp()
	color_ramp = _fade_ramp()


## A solid little square stands in for a sprite: no image asset needed.
func _make_dot() -> Texture2D:
	var image: Image = null
	if ClassDB.class_has_method("Image", "create_empty"):
		image = Image.create_empty(DOT_PX, DOT_PX, false, Image.FORMAT_RGBA8)
	else:
		image = Image.create(DOT_PX, DOT_PX, false, Image.FORMAT_RGBA8)
	image.fill(Color(1, 1, 1, 1))
	return ImageTexture.create_from_image(image)


## Colours are picked per particle, so one burst reads as a mix of tile colours.
func _tile_ramp() -> Gradient:
	var ramp := Gradient.new()
	ramp.offsets = PackedFloat32Array([0.0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0])
	ramp.colors = PackedColorArray([
		ScrambledTheme.tile_color(0), ScrambledTheme.tile_color(1),
		ScrambledTheme.tile_color(2), ScrambledTheme.tile_color(3),
		ScrambledTheme.tile_color(7),
	])
	return ramp


## ...and they fade away as they fall.
func _fade_ramp() -> Gradient:
	var ramp := Gradient.new()
	ramp.offsets = PackedFloat32Array([0.0, 0.65, 1.0])
	ramp.colors = PackedColorArray([
		Color(1, 1, 1, 1), Color(1, 1, 1, 1), Color(1, 1, 1, 0),
	])
	return ramp
```

## File: `res://scenes/word_game/scrambled/ui/confirm_dialog.gd`

```gdscript
class_name ScrambledConfirmDialog
extends Control
## ============================================================
##  CONFIRM DIALOG — "از بازی خارج می‌شوی؟"
##
##  Leaving mid-session asks first. Quitting is forgiving — the points already
##  earned are written by the session manager — but it still ends the run, so
##  the player gets one deliberate question rather than a back tap that steals
##  their word.
##
##  It is laid out with containers rather than the fixed offsets the screen
##  used to compute by hand: a CenterContainer keeps the card centred at any
##  window size, and the card's own MarginContainer keeps its text off the
##  frame. Every look comes from a theme variation (`ScrambledDialogCard`,
##  `ScrambledDialog*` labels, `ScrambledDialogButton` / `ScrambledDangerButton`),
##  so nothing here needs re-applying on a theme toggle.
##
##  Nothing is written here. The dialog only reports which answer it was given.
## ============================================================

signal confirmed()
signal cancelled()

const OPEN_FADE_TIME := 0.18

@onready var _title: Label = $Center/Card/Margin/Column/Title
@onready var _body: Label = $Center/Card/Margin/Column/Body
@onready var _stay: Button = $Center/Card/Margin/Column/Choices/Stay
@onready var _leave: Button = $Center/Card/Margin/Column/Choices/Leave


func _ready() -> void:
	visible = false
	_stay.pressed.connect(_on_stay_pressed)
	_leave.pressed.connect(_on_leave_pressed)
	MenuStyle.wire_microinteractions(_stay)
	MenuStyle.wire_microinteractions(_leave)


func is_open() -> bool:
	return visible


## Asks the question. `body` differs by mode, because what is at stake does:
## a lesson loses its practice, the day keeps its points.
func open(title: String, body: String) -> void:
	_title.text = title
	_body.text = body
	visible = true
	modulate.a = 0.0
	var tw := create_tween()
	tw.tween_property(self, "modulate:a", 1.0, OPEN_FADE_TIME) \
		.set_trans(Tween.TRANS_QUAD).set_ease(Tween.EASE_OUT)
	Sfx.click()


func close() -> void:
	visible = false


func _on_stay_pressed() -> void:
	close()
	cancelled.emit()


## Leaving is the screen's to carry out: it has a session to end and a host to
## tell, so the dialog only reports the answer.
func _on_leave_pressed() -> void:
	confirmed.emit()
```

## File: `res://scenes/word_game/scrambled/ui/gameplay_actions.gd`

```gdscript
class_name ScrambledGameplayActions
extends HBoxContainer
## ============================================================
##  GAMEPLAY ACTIONS — the two ways out of a word that will not come.
##
##  «راهنما» costs points and hands over the meaning; «یک حرف» puts one letter
##  of the answer into its slot. Both are only ever ASKED for: the buttons
##  announce the request and the screen decides whether it may be granted — a
##  component never reaches into the session (per the project's UI rules).
##
##  The buttons wear the game's `Scrambled*Button` theme variations, so their
##  candy look lives with the rest of the game's styling and this script owns
##  only the gesture. It has no apply_theme() for the same reason.
##
##  The hint button does not exist until the word has been going long enough.
##  Arriving on its own is the whole point of that delay, so the entrance is
##  animated here, with the button it belongs to.
## ============================================================

signal hint_requested()
signal reveal_requested()

## The hint button arrives from this scale, opening out with TRANS_BACK.
const HINT_ARRIVE_FROM := 0.6
const HINT_ARRIVE_TIME := 0.4
## A couple of soft wiggles, so the eye finds the button that just appeared.
const WIGGLE_GAP := 0.45
const WIGGLE_ANGLE := 0.035

@onready var _hint: Button = $Hint
@onready var _reveal: Button = $Reveal


func _ready() -> void:
	_hint.pressed.connect(func() -> void: hint_requested.emit())
	_reveal.pressed.connect(func() -> void: reveal_requested.emit())
	# Both are buttons: the same hover-lift / press-squash the rest of the app
	# wears. (The scale is a micro-interaction, not a look, so it stays code.)
	MenuStyle.wire_microinteractions(_hint)
	MenuStyle.wire_microinteractions(_reveal)


## The word has been going long enough: the hint button arrives on its own.
func reveal_hint() -> void:
	_hint.pivot_offset = _hint.size * 0.5
	_hint.scale = Vector2(HINT_ARRIVE_FROM, HINT_ARRIVE_FROM)
	_hint.visible = true
	var tw := create_tween()
	tw.tween_property(_hint, "scale", Vector2.ONE, HINT_ARRIVE_TIME) \
		.set_trans(Tween.TRANS_BACK).set_ease(Tween.EASE_OUT)
	var wiggle := create_tween().set_loops(2)
	wiggle.tween_interval(WIGGLE_GAP)
	wiggle.tween_property(_hint, "rotation", WIGGLE_ANGLE, 0.16).set_trans(Tween.TRANS_SINE)
	wiggle.tween_property(_hint, "rotation", -WIGGLE_ANGLE, 0.22).set_trans(Tween.TRANS_SINE)
	wiggle.tween_property(_hint, "rotation", 0.0, 0.16).set_trans(Tween.TRANS_SINE)
	Sfx.reward()


## The hint has been taken: the button has done its job and steps aside.
func hide_hint() -> void:
	_hint.visible = false
	_hint.scale = Vector2(HINT_ARRIVE_FROM, HINT_ARRIVE_FROM)
	_hint.rotation = 0.0
```

```gdscript
class_name ScrambledGameplayChips
extends HBoxContainer
## ============================================================
##  GAMEPLAY CHIPS — where the run stands, in four pills.
##
##  Which word of the day is in play, which mode is being played, what the
##  current word is still worth, and the points banked so far. It is a
##  component scene of its own (per the project's UI rules) because it is the
##  one part of the screen the board never has to know about: the screen hands
##  it the numbers and it decides the words.
##
##  Each pill wears a `ScrambledChip*` THEME VARIATION, so its look lives with
##  the rest of the game's styling in ScrambledTheme.build_theme() — this
##  component owns only what the chips SAY, never how they look. That is also
##  why it has no apply_theme(): a theme swap repaints it like every other
##  themed node.
##
##  A practice lesson keeps its score chips hidden — a lesson awards nothing,
##  so an «امتیاز» pill there would be a promise the game does not keep.
## ============================================================

@onready var _progress: Label = $Progress
@onready var _mode: Label = $Mode
@onready var _worth: Label = $Worth
@onready var _score: Label = $Score


## "کلمه ۳ از ۵" — a practice lesson reads the very same line, which is why the
## wording is not decided here.
func set_progress(current_index: int, total: int) -> void:
	_progress.text = "کلمه %s از %s" % [
		MenuStyle.persian_digits(str(current_index)),
		MenuStyle.persian_digits(str(total)),
	]


func set_mode(text: String) -> void:
	_mode.text = text


func set_points(points: int) -> void:
	_score.text = "امتیاز: %s" % MenuStyle.persian_digits(str(points))


## `hinted` changes the caption rather than the number: the same word is worth
## less once its meaning has been read, and saying so is the point.
func set_worth(worth: int, hinted: bool) -> void:
	_worth.text = "%s %s" % [
		"با راهنما:" if hinted else "ارزش:",
		MenuStyle.persian_digits(str(worth)),
	]


## The two score chips belong to the day's competition only.
func set_competition(on: bool) -> void:
	_score.visible = on
	_worth.visible = on
```

## File: `res://scenes/word_game/scrambled/ui/gameplay_timer.gd`

```gdscript
class_name ScrambledGameplayTimer
extends HBoxContainer
## ============================================================
##  GAMEPLAY TIMER — the word's clock, as a bar and a readout.
##
##  The bar fills towards a limit the SCREEN chooses, because the two modes
##  count towards different things: a lesson counts towards its hint, the day's
##  competition towards the slowest score band. The colour arrives the same way
##  — the bar only draws what it is told.
##
##  Its SHAPE is the theme's (`ScrambledTimerBar`); only its COLOUR is the
##  clock's own reading, because the colour IS the information: green while the
##  word is worth the top band, amber and red as the bands fall away. So the
##  theme's fill is copied once — corners and all — and the copy is what gets
##  recoloured, which is the smallest override that can express a live reading.
##  The readout needs nothing at all: the app's default label font and colour
##  are already right.
## ============================================================

@onready var _bar: ProgressBar = $Bar
@onready var _time: Label = $Time

## A copy of the theme's fill, kept so the clock can repaint it in place.
var _fill: StyleBoxFlat = null
## Last colour handed to the fill, so an unchanged colour is not rewritten on
## every frame of the timer.
var _last_color := Color(0, 0, 0, 0)


func _ready() -> void:
	# The bar's SHAPE is the theme's (`ScrambledTimerBar`) and only its COLOUR
	# is the clock's own reading, because the colour IS the information. So the
	# theme's fill is copied once — corners and all — and the copy is what gets
	# recoloured, which is the smallest override that can express a live reading.
	#
	# Nothing re-reads the shape on a theme toggle: the shape is the same in
	# both themes, and re-registering the override from inside the notification
	# it fires would recurse forever. The track behind the fill is theme-drawn
	# with no override at all, so it does follow the toggle.
	_fill = (get_theme_stylebox("fill") as StyleBoxFlat).duplicate()
	add_theme_stylebox_override("fill", _fill)


## Fills towards `limit` and paints the fill `color`. Called every frame, so it
## writes nothing that has not changed.
func set_elapsed(elapsed: float, limit: float, color: Color) -> void:
	_bar.value = clampf(elapsed / maxf(limit, 1.0) * 100.0, 0.0, 100.0)
	_time.text = format_clock(elapsed)
	if color == _last_color:
		return
	_last_color = color
	if _fill != null:
		_fill.bg_color = color


## «۱:۰۵» — Persian digits, minutes:seconds. Public because a session's average
## time is read out with the same shape.
static func format_clock(seconds: float) -> String:
	var total := int(floor(seconds))
	return "%s:%s" % [
		MenuStyle.persian_digits(str(int(floor(float(total) / 60.0)))),
		MenuStyle.persian_digits("%02d" % (total % 60)),
	]
```

```gdscript
class_name ScrambledHintCard
extends PanelContainer
## ============================================================
##  HINT CARD — the meaning of the word, dealt like a printed card.
##
##  The English meaning is the hint (that is what a spelling game may give
##  away); the Persian meaning sits underneath as a second hand, and in the
##  day's competition a line says what the word is now worth.
##
##  Its whole look — the cream paper, the green frame, and the four label
##  voices on it — is declared in the theme as `ScrambledHintCard` and the
##  `ScrambledHint*` label variations, so this script owns only the meaning it
##  shows and the animation that deals it in. The card is deliberately painted
##  from fixed colours rather than the palette: it must read the same in both
##  themes, like a card dealt onto the board.
##
##  The entrance lives here with the thing it animates (per the project's UI
##  rules) — it is the one moment on this screen that should feel like
##  something being dealt.
## ============================================================

## The card lands slightly small and opens out, TRANS_BACK.
const ENTER_FROM := 0.86
const ENTER_TIME := 0.34
const ENTER_FADE_TIME := 0.22

@onready var _meaning: Label = $Column/Meaning
@onready var _persian: Label = $Column/Persian
@onready var _worth: Label = $Column/Worth


func _ready() -> void:
	visible = false
	resized.connect(func() -> void: pivot_offset = size * 0.5)


func is_shown() -> bool:
	return visible


## Deals the card in: the meaning first, the Persian one under it, and — in the
## competition — a line about what reading it costs.
func show_hint(meaning: String, meaning_fa: String, worth_text: String) -> void:
	_meaning.text = meaning if not meaning.is_empty() else "—"
	_persian.text = meaning_fa
	_persian.visible = not meaning_fa.is_empty()
	_worth.text = worth_text
	_worth.visible = not worth_text.is_empty()

	pivot_offset = size * 0.5
	scale = Vector2(ENTER_FROM, ENTER_FROM)
	modulate.a = 0.0
	visible = true
	var tw := create_tween()
	tw.set_parallel(true)
	tw.tween_property(self, "scale", Vector2.ONE, ENTER_TIME) \
		.set_trans(Tween.TRANS_BACK).set_ease(Tween.EASE_OUT)
	tw.tween_property(self, "modulate:a", 1.0, ENTER_FADE_TIME) \
		.set_trans(Tween.TRANS_QUAD).set_ease(Tween.EASE_OUT)


## Takes the card away with no animation: used when a new word is dealt, where
## the board is already moving and a second animation would fight it.
func hide_hint() -> void:
	visible = false
	scale = Vector2.ONE
	modulate.a = 1.0
```

## File: `res://scenes/word_game/scrambled/ui/praise_overlay.gd`

```gdscript
class_name ScrambledPraiseOverlay
extends Control
## ============================================================
##  PRAISE OVERLAY — the "well done" the board never has to know about.
##
##  Two floating pieces of feedback live here: the big «آفرین!» that lands when
##  a word is spelled, and the "+۶۰" that rises off the board as the points are
##  banked. They deliberately sit ABOVE the layout in their own full-rect
##  overlay, because they are not part of the board's flow — nothing should
##  move when they appear, and they must not swallow a drag aimed at the row
##  (hence the overlay and its labels are all mouse-ignoring).
##
##  Both wear a theme variation (`ScrambledPraise`, `ScrambledPoints`), so the
##  only thing left in this script is the movement — and nothing to re-apply on
##  a theme toggle.
##
##  The lines are chosen here: which praise to say is a presentation decision,
##  not something the screen that awards a word should have to make.
## ============================================================

const LINES := ["آفرین!", "عالی بود!", "درسته!", "چه سریع!"]
## The praise lands from here and springs open, then breathes.
const PRAISE_FROM := 0.5
const PRAISE_LAND_TIME := 0.36
const PRAISE_BREATHE_TIME := 0.9
const PRAISE_BREATHE_TO := 0.97
## The points rise this far, in pixels, while they fade. The resting place is
## pinned by these two, so a burst after a burst rises from the same spot
## instead of drifting off the top of the screen.
const POINTS_RISE := 170.0
const POINTS_TIME := 1.1
const POINTS_REST_TOP := -140.0
const POINTS_REST_BOTTOM := -50.0

@onready var _praise: Label = $Praise
@onready var _points: Label = $Points


## Lands a random line of praise.
func celebrate() -> void:
	_praise.text = LINES[randi() % LINES.size()]
	_praise.visible = true
	_praise.scale = Vector2(PRAISE_FROM, PRAISE_FROM)
	var tw := create_tween()
	tw.tween_property(_praise, "scale", Vector2.ONE, PRAISE_LAND_TIME) \
		.set_trans(Tween.TRANS_BACK).set_ease(Tween.EASE_OUT)
	tw.tween_property(_praise, "scale", Vector2(PRAISE_BREATHE_TO, PRAISE_BREATHE_TO),
		PRAISE_BREATHE_TIME).set_trans(Tween.TRANS_SINE).set_ease(Tween.EASE_IN_OUT)


## "+۶۰" rises off the board and fades — the classic score pop.
func float_points(points: int) -> void:
	_points.text = "+%s" % MenuStyle.persian_digits(str(points))
	_points.visible = true
	_points.modulate.a = 1.0
	_points.offset_top = POINTS_REST_TOP
	_points.offset_bottom = POINTS_REST_BOTTOM
	var tw := create_tween()
	tw.set_parallel(true)
	tw.tween_property(_points, "offset_top", POINTS_REST_TOP - POINTS_RISE, POINTS_TIME) \
		.set_trans(Tween.TRANS_QUAD).set_ease(Tween.EASE_OUT)
	tw.tween_property(_points, "offset_bottom", POINTS_REST_BOTTOM - POINTS_RISE, POINTS_TIME) \
		.set_trans(Tween.TRANS_QUAD).set_ease(Tween.EASE_OUT)
	tw.tween_property(_points, "modulate:a", 0.0, POINTS_TIME) \
		.set_trans(Tween.TRANS_QUAD).set_ease(Tween.EASE_IN)


## Wipes both pieces of feedback, ready for the next word.
func clear() -> void:
	_praise.visible = false
	_praise.scale = Vector2.ONE
	_points.visible = false
	_points.modulate.a = 1.0
```

## File: `res://scenes/word_game/scrambled/ui/tile_preview.gd`

```gdscript
class_name TilePreview
extends Control
## ============================================================
##  TILE PREVIEW — the carried copy of a letter (rule 2: every native
##  drag must hand the player something visible to hold).
##
##  STRUCTURE
##    TilePreview      (this node) — zero-sized anchor, no drawing
##      └── Visual     (TilePreviewVisual) — the candy block itself
##
##  WHY THE ROOT IS ZERO-SIZED: Godot places a drag preview somewhere
##  around the cursor, and the exact offset depends on how the engine
##  treats the preview's own rect. With a zero-sized root both readings
##  collapse to the same result, and the Visual — parked at -(size / 2)
##  inside the root — lands dead centre on the finger. Nothing has to
##  guess, and nothing shifts if the engine's placement changes.
## ============================================================

## The carried copy is inset a little, so the slot it will drop into
## stays readable under the finger.
const PREVIEW_SCALE := 0.92

@onready var _visual: TilePreviewVisual = $Visual


## Builds the carried copy for one letter. `tile_size` is the source
## tile's size.
func configure(letter_text: String, tile_color_index: int, tile_size: float) -> void:
	var visual := _resolve_visual()
	if visual == null:
		return
	visual.letter = letter_text
	visual.color_index = tile_color_index
	visual.set_tile_size(tile_size * PREVIEW_SCALE)


## The Visual may not be resolved yet while the caller is still inside
## the frame that built the preview, so fall back to a lookup instead of
## letting a null reference drop the letter out of the player's hand.
func _resolve_visual() -> TilePreviewVisual:
	if _visual != null and is_instance_valid(_visual):
		return _visual
	return get_node_or_null("Visual") as TilePreviewVisual
```

## File: `res://scenes/word_game/scrambled/ui/tile_preview_visual.gd`

```gdscript
class_name TilePreviewVisual
extends Control
## ============================================================
##  TILE PREVIEW VISUAL — the drawn half of the drag preview.
##
##  Lives as the "Visual" child of TilePreview.tscn. It sits at
##  -(size/2) inside its zero-sized parent, so the block is centred on
##  the cursor no matter which offset convention Godot's drag layer
##  uses for the preview root.
##
##  Why it is a separate node from ScrambledTile: a preview is a
##  *snapshot* of a letter, not a live tile. It must never join the
##  board's slot bookkeeping or answer input, so it carries no drag
##  state — it only knows how to draw one candy block.
## ============================================================

## Same proportions as ScrambledTile, so the carried copy reads as the
## very same object the player picked up.
const CORNER_RATIO := 0.34
const OUTLINE_RATIO := 0.085
const SIDE_RATIO := 0.16
const LETTER_RATIO := 0.62
const MIN_LETTER_SIZE := 18

## The preview floats: a stronger shadow than any resting tile, so it
## reads as "held above the board" rather than "dropped on it".
const PREVIEW_SHADOW_ALPHA := 0.35
const PREVIEW_SHADOW_SIZE := 28
const PREVIEW_SHADOW_OFFSET := Vector2(0.0, 22.0)
const PREVIEW_GLOSS_ALPHA := 0.25

var letter := ""
var color_index := 0
## Slightly transparent so the slot the letter will land in stays visible
## underneath the carried copy.
var _tint := Color(1.0, 1.0, 1.0, 0.94)

var _style := StyleBoxFlat.new()


func _ready() -> void:
	# The preview must never eat the mouse: the Viewport needs the pointer
	# to keep resolving the real drop target underneath it.
	mouse_filter = Control.MOUSE_FILTER_IGNORE
	_refresh()


## Sizes the block and centres it on the parent's origin.
func set_tile_size(px: float) -> void:
	var side_px := maxf(px, 32.0)
	size = Vector2(side_px, side_px)
	position = -size * 0.5
	modulate = _tint
	_refresh()


func _refresh() -> void:
	if size.x <= 0.0:
		return
	_style.set_corner_radius_all(int(maxf(8.0, size.x * CORNER_RATIO)))
	_style.set_border_width_all(0)
	_style.bg_color = ScrambledTheme.TILE_OUTLINE
	_style.shadow_color = Color(0.10, 0.06, 0.20, PREVIEW_SHADOW_ALPHA)
	_style.shadow_size = PREVIEW_SHADOW_SIZE
	_style.shadow_offset = PREVIEW_SHADOW_OFFSET
	queue_redraw()


func _draw() -> void:
	if size.x <= 0.0 or size.y <= 0.0:
		return
	var body := ScrambledTheme.tile_color(color_index)
	var radius := maxf(8.0, size.x * CORNER_RATIO)
	var outline := maxf(2.0, size.x * OUTLINE_RATIO)
	var side := maxf(4.0, size.x * SIDE_RATIO)
	var inner := size - Vector2(outline * 2.0, outline * 2.0)
	if inner.x <= 0.0 or inner.y - side <= 0.0:
		return

	# 1. Dark outline, 2. extruded bottom edge, 3. candy face, 4. gloss —
	#    the exact stack ScrambledTile draws.
	draw_style_box(_style, Rect2(Vector2.ZERO, size))
	draw_style_box(_slab_style(ScrambledTheme.tile_side(body), radius),
		Rect2(Vector2(outline, outline), inner))
	draw_style_box(_slab_style(body, radius),
		Rect2(Vector2(outline, outline), Vector2(inner.x, inner.y - side)))
	var gloss_height := maxf(4.0, (inner.y - side) * 0.30)
	draw_style_box(_slab_style(Color(1, 1, 1, PREVIEW_GLOSS_ALPHA), int(radius * 0.7)),
		Rect2(Vector2(outline + radius * 0.28, outline + radius * 0.20),
			Vector2(inner.x - radius * 0.56, gloss_height)))

	if letter.is_empty():
		return
	var font := MenuStyle.nunito()
	if font == null:
		font = get_theme_default_font()
	if font == null:
		return
	var letter_size := int(maxf(float(MIN_LETTER_SIZE), size.x * LETTER_RATIO))
	var face_center := outline + (inner.y - side) * 0.5
	var ascent := font.get_ascent(letter_size)
	var descent := font.get_descent(letter_size)
	var baseline := face_center + (ascent - descent) * 0.5
	draw_string(font, Vector2(0.0, baseline), letter, HORIZONTAL_ALIGNMENT_CENTER,
		size.x, letter_size, ScrambledTheme.tile_letter(body))


func _slab_style(color: Color, radius: float) -> StyleBoxFlat:
	var style := StyleBoxFlat.new()
	style.set_corner_radius_all(int(radius))
	style.set_border_width_all(0)
	style.bg_color = color
	return style
```

## File: `res://scenes/word_game/scrambled/word_controller.gd`

```gdscript
class_name ScrambledWordController
extends RefCounted
## ============================================================
##  SCRAMBLED WORD CONTROLLER — everything about ONE word of a session.
##
##  Owns the answer, the scrambled starting arrangement and the checks the
##  board runs against them. It is deliberately free of any UI: the board
##  asks it for the letters and whether they are in order, which keeps the
##  trickiest rules testable on their own —
##
##    * a scramble never starts solved when the word allows a different
##      arrangement (a board that is already the answer is no puzzle),
##    * the same seed always produces the same scramble, so the daily
##      challenge deals every player an identical board,
##    * the "near miss" test behind the gentle you-are-almost-there nudge,
##      which never shows the answer.
## ============================================================

## How many shuffles to try before accepting the rare word whose every
## arrangement reads as the answer (a single repeated letter, say).
const SCRAMBLE_TRIES := 24

## The answer in its original spelling.
var word := ""
var meaning := ""
var meaning_fa := ""
var book := 1
var lesson := 1

## The answer, letter by letter, uppercased.
var target: Array = []
## The starting arrangement of the board, letter by letter.
var letters: Array = []
## The seed the current scramble came from (0 = freshly randomised).
var seed_value := 0


## Fills the controller from one word-bank entry and deals its scramble.
func setup(word_data: Dictionary, scramble_seed: int = 0) -> void:
	word = str(word_data.get("word", "")).strip_edges()
	meaning = str(word_data.get("meaning", "")).strip_edges()
	meaning_fa = str(word_data.get("meaning_fa", "")).strip_edges()
	book = int(word_data.get("book", book))
	lesson = int(word_data.get("lesson", lesson))
	target = []
	for ch in word.to_upper():
		target.append(ch)
	rescramble(scramble_seed)


## Rebuilds the starting arrangement. A seed of 0 randomises; any other value
## repeats exactly, which is what makes a daily puzzle comparable.
func rescramble(scramble_seed: int = 0) -> void:
	seed_value = scramble_seed
	letters = target.duplicate()
	if target.size() < 2:
		return

	var rng := RandomNumberGenerator.new()
	if scramble_seed == 0:
		rng.randomize()
	else:
		rng.seed = scramble_seed

	var answer := word.to_upper()
	for attempt in SCRAMBLE_TRIES:
		var candidate := target.duplicate()
		_shuffle(candidate, rng)
		if letters_to_text(candidate) != answer:
			letters = candidate
			return
	# Every arrangement reads as the answer (the word has next to no distinct
	# letters): keep the original order and let the player have an easy win.


func letter_count() -> int:
	return target.size()


## The answer as text, for the moment the word is finally shown.
func solution() -> String:
	return word.to_upper()


## True when the letters currently on the board spell the word.
func is_solved(current: Array) -> bool:
	if current.size() != target.size():
		return false
	for i in target.size():
		if str(current[i]).to_upper() != target[i]:
			return false
	return true


## Positions whose letter does not match the answer yet.
func misplaced(current: Array) -> Array:
	var out: Array = []
	for i in mini(target.size(), current.size()):
		if str(current[i]).to_upper() != target[i]:
			out.append(i)
	return out


## True when only one or two positions are wrong: the point where a gentle
## "nearly there" nudge helps instead of giving the answer away.
func is_near_miss(current: Array) -> bool:
	var wrong := misplaced(current)
	return wrong.size() >= 1 and wrong.size() <= 2


## -------------------------------------------------------------- helpers --
static func letters_to_text(letters_in: Array) -> String:
	var out := ""
	for ch in letters_in:
		out += str(ch)
	return out


static func _shuffle(list: Array, rng: RandomNumberGenerator) -> void:
	for i in range(list.size() - 1, 0, -1):
		var j := rng.randi_range(0, i)
		var held = list[i]
		list[i] = list[j]
		list[j] = held
```

## File: `res://scenes/word_game/word_game.gd`

```gdscript
extends "res://autoload/BackButtonHandler.gd"
# ============================================================
# WORD GAME HUB — بازی با کلمات
# Entry hub for the three word-based game modes:
#   کلمه روز / بازی معنی / بازی املا
# ============================================================

const SCENE_WORD_OF_DAY := "res://scenes/word_game/WordOfDay.tscn"
const SCENE_MEANING := "res://scenes/word_game/MeaningQuiz.tscn"
const SCENE_SPELLING := "res://scenes/word_game/SpellingGame.tscn"
@onready var back_button: Button = $HeaderBar/HeaderContent/BackButton
@onready var word_of_day_button: Button = $Content/WordOfDayButton
@onready var meaning_button: Button = $Content/MeaningButton
@onready var spelling_button: Button = $Content/SpellingButton
@onready var word_of_day_label: Label = $Content/WordOfDayButton/Margin/Row/Title
@onready var meaning_label: Label = $Content/MeaningButton/Margin/Row/Title
@onready var spelling_label: Label = $Content/SpellingButton/Margin/Row/Title

func _ready() -> void:
	for label: Label in [word_of_day_label, meaning_label, spelling_label]:
		label.self_modulate = Color.WHITE
		label.modulate = Color.WHITE
	word_of_day_button.pressed.connect(_on_word_of_day_pressed)
	meaning_button.pressed.connect(_on_meaning_pressed)
	spelling_button.pressed.connect(_on_spelling_pressed)
	if back_button != null:
		back_button.pressed.connect(_on_android_back_pressed)
	_wire_button_animations()


############################################################
# BUTTON ANIMATIONS
############################################################
## Hover-lift / press-squash micro-interactions (same design language as
## the main-menu cards) on every game-mode button.
func _wire_button_animations() -> void:
	for btn: Button in [word_of_day_button, meaning_button, spelling_button]:
		btn.pivot_offset = btn.size / 2.0
		btn.resized.connect(_update_mode_button_pivot.bind(btn))
		btn.mouse_entered.connect(_on_mode_button_hovered.bind(btn))
		btn.mouse_exited.connect(_on_mode_button_exited.bind(btn))
		btn.button_down.connect(_animate_mode_button.bind(btn, Vector2(0.97, 0.97)))
		btn.button_up.connect(_on_mode_button_up.bind(btn))
	_play_entrance_animation()


func _update_mode_button_pivot(btn: Button) -> void:
	btn.pivot_offset = btn.size / 2.0


func _on_mode_button_hovered(btn: Button) -> void:
	if not btn.button_pressed:
		_animate_mode_button(btn, Vector2(1.03, 1.03))


func _on_mode_button_exited(btn: Button) -> void:
	if not btn.button_pressed:
		_animate_mode_button(btn, Vector2.ONE)


func _on_mode_button_up(btn: Button) -> void:
	var target_scale: Vector2 = Vector2(1.03, 1.03) if btn.is_hovered() else Vector2.ONE
	_animate_mode_button(btn, target_scale)


func _animate_mode_button(btn: Button, target_scale: Vector2) -> void:
	if btn.has_meta("word_game_scale_tween"):
		var old_tween: Tween = btn.get_meta("word_game_scale_tween") as Tween
		if old_tween != null and old_tween.is_valid():
			old_tween.kill()
	var tween: Tween = btn.create_tween()
	btn.set_meta("word_game_scale_tween", tween)
	tween.tween_property(btn, "scale", target_scale, 0.14).set_trans(Tween.TRANS_BACK).set_ease(Tween.EASE_OUT)


## Staggered entrance: each button fades in and rises from slightly below,
## then pops (TRANS_BACK) — mirrors the main menu's intro feel.
func _play_entrance_animation() -> void:
	var buttons: Array[Button] = [word_of_day_button, meaning_button, spelling_button]
	for btn in buttons:
		btn.modulate.a = 0.0
		btn.position.y += 40.0

	await get_tree().process_frame
	if not is_inside_tree():
		return

	for i in buttons.size():
		var btn: Button = buttons[i]
		var tw := create_tween()
		tw.tween_interval(0.08 * i)
		tw.tween_property(btn, "modulate:a", 1.0, 0.32) \
			.set_trans(Tween.TRANS_QUAD).set_ease(Tween.EASE_OUT)
		tw.parallel().tween_property(btn, "position:y", btn.position.y - 40.0, 0.32) \
			.set_trans(Tween.TRANS_QUAD).set_ease(Tween.EASE_OUT)

	# Idle scale pulse intentionally disabled; entrance and hover/press
	# micro-interactions remain active.


func _on_android_back_pressed() -> void:
	TransitionManager.change_scene("res://scenes/main_menu/MainMenu.tscn")


func _on_word_of_day_pressed() -> void:
	TransitionManager.change_scene(SCENE_WORD_OF_DAY)


func _on_meaning_pressed() -> void:
	TransitionManager.change_scene(SCENE_MEANING)


func _on_spelling_pressed() -> void:
	TransitionManager.change_scene(SCENE_SPELLING)
```

## File: `res://scenes/word_game/word_of_day.gd`

```gdscript
extends "res://autoload/BackButtonHandler.gd"
# ============================================================
# کلمه روز — the daily Wordle puzzle.
#
# This scene hosts the puzzle content in wordle/WordleScreen.tscn. Header
# controls are omitted so the daily puzzle can use the full screen; Android
# back remains supported by BackButtonHandler.
# ============================================================

const SCENE_WORD_GAME := "res://scenes/word_game/WordGameHub.tscn"

## The instanced puzzle content provides the panel-close API used by Android
## back, without this scene needing to know its concrete game type.
@onready var game_content: Node = $Game


func _on_android_back_pressed() -> void:
	if game_content != null and game_content.has_method("close_panels") \
			and bool(game_content.call("close_panels")):
		return
	TransitionManager.change_scene(SCENE_WORD_GAME)
```

## File: `res://scenes/word_game/WordGameHub.gd`

```gdscript
extends "res://autoload/BackButtonHandler.gd"
class_name WordGameHub

const LEARNING_SCENE: String = "res://scenes/word_game/WordGameLearning.tscn"
const DAILY_SCENE: String = "res://scenes/word_game/DailyWordGame.tscn"
const MAIN_MENU_SCENE: String = "res://scenes/main_menu/MainMenu.tscn"
const BUTTON_PRESSED_SCALE: float = 0.94
const BUTTON_PRESS_DURATION: float = 0.12
const BUTTON_RELEASE_DURATION: float = 0.20

@onready var _back_button: Button = $HeaderBar/HeaderContent/BackButton
@onready var _learning_button: Button = $Scroll/MainMargin/MainColumn/ModeButtons/LearningButton
@onready var _daily_button: Button = $Scroll/MainMargin/MainColumn/ModeButtons/DailyButton
@onready var _daily_board_button: Button = $Scroll/MainMargin/MainColumn/Tabs/DailyBoardButton
@onready var _lifetime_button: Button = $Scroll/MainMargin/MainColumn/Tabs/LifetimeButton
@onready var _status: Label = $Scroll/MainMargin/MainColumn/Status
@onready var _entries: VBoxContainer = $Scroll/MainMargin/MainColumn/Entries

var _daily_selected: bool = true
var _board_request_id: int = 0
var _button_tweens: Dictionary = {}

func _ready() -> void:
	_back_button.pressed.connect(_on_back_pressed)
	for button: Button in [_learning_button, _daily_button, _daily_board_button, _lifetime_button]:
		button.pivot_offset = button.size / 2.0
		button.resized.connect(_on_button_resized.bind(button))
		button.button_down.connect(_on_button_down.bind(button))
		button.button_up.connect(_on_button_up.bind(button))

	_learning_button.pressed.connect(_on_learning_pressed)
	_daily_button.pressed.connect(_on_daily_pressed)
	_daily_board_button.pressed.connect(_on_daily_board_pressed)
	_lifetime_button.pressed.connect(_on_lifetime_board_pressed)
	_load_board()

func _on_button_resized(button: Button) -> void:
	button.pivot_offset = button.size / 2.0

func _on_button_down(button: Button) -> void:
	_animate_button_scale(button, BUTTON_PRESSED_SCALE, BUTTON_PRESS_DURATION, Tween.EASE_OUT)

func _on_button_up(button: Button) -> void:
	_animate_button_scale(button, 1.0, BUTTON_RELEASE_DURATION, Tween.EASE_OUT)

func _animate_button_scale(button: Button, target_scale: float, duration: float, easing: Tween.EaseType) -> void:
	var button_id: int = button.get_instance_id()
	var previous_tween: Tween = _button_tweens.get(button_id) as Tween
	if previous_tween != null and previous_tween.is_running():
		previous_tween.kill()

	var tween: Tween = create_tween()
	tween.set_trans(Tween.TRANS_QUAD)
	tween.set_ease(easing)
	tween.tween_property(button, "scale", Vector2(target_scale, target_scale), duration)
	_button_tweens[button_id] = tween

func _on_learning_pressed() -> void:
	TransitionManager.change_scene(LEARNING_SCENE)

func _on_daily_pressed() -> void:
	TransitionManager.change_scene(DAILY_SCENE)

func _on_daily_board_pressed() -> void:
	_daily_selected = true
	_load_board()

func _on_lifetime_board_pressed() -> void:
	_daily_selected = false
	_load_board()

func _update_tab_selection() -> void:
	# Selection state only — visuals are Inspector-owned.
	# In WordGameHub.tscn set toggle_mode = true on both tab buttons and
	# style button_pressed differently from normal to show selection.
	_daily_board_button.button_pressed = _daily_selected
	_lifetime_button.button_pressed = not _daily_selected


func _load_board() -> void:
	_board_request_id += 1
	for child: Node in _entries.get_children():
		_entries.remove_child(child)
		child.queue_free()
	_update_tab_selection()
	if not API.is_configured() or not API.is_logged_in():
		_status.text = "برای مشاهدهٔ رتبه‌بندی جهانی، ورود و اتصال اینترنت لازم است."
		return
	var request_id: int = _board_request_id
	_status.text = "در حال دریافت رتبه‌بندی رسمی از سرور…"
	if _daily_selected:
		API.fetch_daily_leaderboard(50, 0, func(ok: bool, data: Dictionary) -> void: _on_board_loaded(request_id, true, ok, data))
	else:
		API.fetch_lifetime_leaderboard(50, 0, func(ok: bool, data: Dictionary) -> void: _on_board_loaded(request_id, false, ok, data))

func _on_board_loaded(request_id: int, was_daily: bool, ok: bool, data: Dictionary) -> void:
	if request_id != _board_request_id or was_daily != _daily_selected:
		return
	if not ok:
		_status.text = "رتبه‌بندی از سرور دریافت نشد؛ لطفاً اتصال را بررسی کنید."
		return
	var period: String = "امروز · %s" % str(data.get("date", "")) if _daily_selected else "مجموع امتیازهای ثبت‌شده"
	var self_row: Variant = data.get("self", null)
	if self_row is Dictionary:
		var self_data: Dictionary = self_row
		_status.text = "%s\nرتبهٔ شما: %s · امتیاز: %s" % [period, str(self_data.get("rank", "—")), str(self_data.get("score", 0))]
	else:
		_status.text = "%s\nهنوز امتیازی در این بازه ندارید." % period
	var rows: Array = data.get("entries", [])
	if rows.is_empty():
		_entries.add_child(_make_label("هنوز بازیکنی در این بازه امتیاز ثبت نکرده است."))
		return
	for raw: Variant in rows:
		if not raw is Dictionary:
			continue
		var entry: Dictionary = raw
		var panel: PanelContainer = PanelContainer.new()
		panel.name = "SelfRow" if bool(entry.get("isSelf", false)) else "Row"
		var row: HBoxContainer = HBoxContainer.new()
		panel.add_child(row)
		row.add_child(_make_label("#%s" % str(entry.get("rank", "—"))))
		row.add_child(_make_label(str(entry.get("name", "بازیکن"))))
		var score: Label = _make_label(str(entry.get("score", 0)))
		score.size_flags_horizontal = Control.SIZE_EXPAND_FILL
		row.add_child(score)
		_entries.add_child(panel)

func _make_label(value: String) -> Label:
	var label: Label = Label.new()
	label.text = value
	label.size_flags_horizontal = Control.SIZE_EXPAND_FILL
	label.horizontal_alignment = HORIZONTAL_ALIGNMENT_CENTER
	label.autowrap_mode = TextServer.AUTOWRAP_WORD_SMART
	return label

func _on_back_pressed() -> void:
	TransitionManager.change_scene(MAIN_MENU_SCENE)

func _on_android_back_pressed() -> void:
	_on_back_pressed()
```

## File: `res://scenes/word_game/WordGameLearning.gd`

```gdscript
extends "res://autoload/BackButtonHandler.gd"
class_name WordGameLearning

const MEANING_SCENE: String = "res://scenes/word_game/MeaningQuiz.tscn"
const SCRAMBLED_SCENE: String = "res://scenes/word_game/scrambled/ScrambledWords.tscn"
const HUB_SCENE: String = "res://scenes/word_game/WordGameHub.tscn"

@onready var _background: ColorRect = $Background
@onready var _back_button: Button = $HeaderBar/HeaderContent/BackButton
@onready var _wordef_button: Button = $MainMargin/MainColumn/WordefButton
@onready var _unscramble_button: Button = $MainMargin/MainColumn/UnscrambleButton

func _ready() -> void:
	_background.color = MenuStyle.c("bg")
	MenuStyle.style_button(_wordef_button, "primary")
	MenuStyle.style_button(_unscramble_button, "secondary")
	_back_button.pressed.connect(_on_back_pressed)
	_wordef_button.pressed.connect(_on_wordef_pressed)
	_unscramble_button.pressed.connect(_on_unscramble_pressed)

func _on_back_pressed() -> void:
	TransitionManager.change_scene(HUB_SCENE)

func _on_wordef_pressed() -> void:
	TransitionManager.change_scene(MEANING_SCENE)

func _on_unscramble_pressed() -> void:
	TransitionManager.change_scene(SCRAMBLED_SCENE)

func _on_android_back_pressed() -> void:
	TransitionManager.change_scene(HUB_SCENE)
```
