## File: `res://tests/test_final_exams.gd`

```gdscript
extends Node
## ============================================================
##  FINAL EXAMS DATA TESTS
##
##  Validates the "امتحانات نهایی" content and the /40 scoring
##  model without needing the UI:
##    * the manifest parses and every referenced exam JSON exists
##    * each exam loads, has blocks, and every listening block's
##      audio file actually exists on disk
##    * every gradable block (points > 0) has an exercise_id and a
##      gradable type — the grader ignores anything else
##    * the sum of gradable points is within (0, 40], so the /40
##      scaling in final_exam.gd never divides by zero or exceeds
##      the maximum
##    * a fully-correct run always yields exactly 40
## ============================================================

const MANIFEST_PATH: String = "res://data/final_exams/manifest.json"
const GRADABLE_EXCLUDED: Array[String] = ["open_ended", "pronunciation", "writing", "passage", "reading"]
const SCORE_MAX: float = 40.0


func test_manifest_has_years_and_exams() -> void:
	var manifest: Dictionary = _read_json(MANIFEST_PATH)
	assert(not manifest.is_empty(), "manifest.json did not parse")
	var years: Array = manifest.get("years", [])
	assert(not years.is_empty(), "manifest has no years")
	for year in years:
		assert(not year.get("exams", []).is_empty(), "year %s has no exams" % year.get("id", "?"))


func test_each_exam_is_valid() -> void:
	var manifest: Dictionary = _read_json(MANIFEST_PATH)
	var years: Array = manifest.get("years", [])
	var exam_count: int = 0
	for year in years:
		for exam in year.get("exams", []):
			_validate_exam(exam)
			exam_count += 1
	assert(exam_count > 0, "no exams validated")


func test_scenes_load() -> void:
	assert(load("res://scenes/exam/FinalExams.tscn") != null, "FinalExams.tscn failed to load")
	assert(load("res://scenes/exam/FinalExamList.tscn") != null, "FinalExamList.tscn failed to load")
	assert(load("res://scenes/exam/FinalExam.tscn") != null, "FinalExam.tscn failed to load")


func test_runner_scores_out_of_40() -> void:
	AppRouter.set_args({
		"exam_json": "res://tests/fixtures/final_exam_min.json",
		"title_fa": "آزمون آزمایشی",
	})
	var scene: Node = load("res://scenes/exam/FinalExam.tscn").instantiate()
	add_child(scene)
	assert(scene.get("_check_btn") != null, "runner did not create the global check button")
	# Grade with nothing answered: the popup must still be on the /40 scale.
	scene.call("_on_check_pressed")
	var score_text: String = _find_score_text(scene)
	assert(score_text.ends_with("/ ۴۰"), "score popup is not out of 40: '%s'" % score_text)
	scene.queue_free()


func _find_score_text(root: Node) -> String:
	for child in root.get_children():
		if child is Label and str((child as Label).text).contains("/ ۴۰"):
			return str((child as Label).text)
		var found: String = _find_score_text(child)
		if found != "":
			return found
	return ""


func _validate_exam(exam: Dictionary) -> void:
	var exam_id: String = str(exam.get("id", "?"))
	var path: String = str(exam.get("json", ""))
	assert(path != "" and FileAccess.file_exists(path), "exam %s: missing json %s" % [exam_id, path])

	var data: Dictionary = _read_json(path)
	assert(not data.is_empty(), "exam %s: json did not parse" % exam_id)

	var audio: String = str(data.get("audio", ""))
	assert(audio != "" and FileAccess.file_exists(audio), "exam %s: missing audio %s" % [exam_id, audio])

	var blocks: Array = data.get("blocks", [])
	assert(not blocks.is_empty(), "exam %s: no blocks" % exam_id)

	var gradable_points: float = 0.0
	for block in blocks:
		var type: String = str(block.get("type", ""))
		if type == "h4":
			continue
		if bool(block.get("show_audio", false)):
			var block_audio: String = str(block.get("audio", ""))
			assert(block_audio != "" and FileAccess.file_exists(block_audio),
				"exam %s: listening block audio missing %s" % [exam_id, block_audio])

		var points: float = float(block.get("points", 0))
		if points > 0.0:
			assert(str(block.get("exercise_id", "")) != "",
				"exam %s: gradable %s block has no exercise_id" % [exam_id, type])
			assert(not GRADABLE_EXCLUDED.has(type),
				"exam %s: non-gradable type %s carries points" % [exam_id, type])
			gradable_points += points

	assert(gradable_points > 0.0, "exam %s: no gradable points" % exam_id)
	assert(gradable_points <= SCORE_MAX + 0.001,
		"exam %s: gradable points %.1f exceed the maximum" % [exam_id, gradable_points])

	# A perfect run scales to exactly 40.
	var score: float = SCORE_MAX * gradable_points / gradable_points
	assert(is_equal_approx(score, SCORE_MAX), "exam %s: perfect score != 40" % exam_id)


func _read_json(path: String) -> Dictionary:
	if not FileAccess.file_exists(path):
		return {}
	var text: String = FileAccess.get_file_as_string(path)
	var data: Variant = JSON.parse_string(text)
	if data is Dictionary:
		return data
	return {}
```

## File: `res://tests/test_gloss_card.gd`

```gdscript
extends Node
## ============================================================
##  GLOSSY MENU CARD — regression test for the shiny section cards.
##
##  The lesson menu's section cards are glossy buttons: a raised face carrying a
##  whisper of the section colour (MenuTheme.gloss_body) with a sheen overlay on
##  top of it (GlossSheen + gloss_sheen.gdshader) that brightens on hover and
##  flattens while pressed.
##
##  What must stay true:
##    • a glossy card carries exactly ONE coating, tinted with its accent and
##      masked with the card's own corner radius,
##    • the coating never eats the card's clicks and paints under its content,
##    • restyling (a theme change) reuses the coating instead of stacking one,
##    • hover / press / release drive the shine,
##    • the shine actually paints — a bright band at the top, the shaded bottom
##      and rounded corners that keep their curve.
##
##  Run with run_tests on this file.
## ============================================================

const GlossSheenScript := preload("res://ui/widgets/gloss_sheen.gd")
const LESSON_MENU_SCENE: PackedScene = preload("res://scenes/lesson_menu/LessonMenu.tscn")

const ACCENT := Color("#4C8DF6")
const OTHER_ACCENT := Color("#E4572E")
const RADIUS := 26
## Sized like a real section card, so the radius mask is measured against the
## proportions the sheen shader is tuned for.
const CARD_SIZE := Vector2(600, 150)


func test_card_carries_exactly_one_shine_coating() -> void:
	var card: Button = await _glossy_card(ACCENT)
	var glosses: Array[GlossSheen] = _glosses(card)
	_check(glosses.size() == 1, "the card carries exactly one shine coating (%d)" % glosses.size())
	if glosses.is_empty():
		await _discard(card)
		return

	var gloss: GlossSheen = glosses[0]
	_check(gloss.get_script() == GlossSheenScript, "the coating is a GlossSheen")
	_check(
		gloss.mouse_filter == Control.MOUSE_FILTER_IGNORE,
		"the coating never swallows the card's clicks"
	)
	_check(
		gloss.get_index() == 0,
		"the coating paints under the icon chip and the labels"
	)
	_check(
		gloss.size.is_equal_approx(CARD_SIZE),
		"the coating covers the whole face (%s vs %s)" % [str(gloss.size), str(CARD_SIZE)]
	)

	await _discard(card)


func test_shine_is_tinted_and_masked_like_the_card() -> void:
	var card: Button = await _glossy_card(ACCENT)
	var gloss: GlossSheen = _glosses(card)[0]
	var mat: ShaderMaterial = gloss.material as ShaderMaterial
	_check(mat != null, "the coating has a material")
	_check(mat.shader != null, "the coating runs a shader")

	_check(
		(mat.get_shader_parameter("tint") as Color) == ACCENT,
		"the shine is tinted with the section accent"
	)
	_check(
		is_equal_approx(float(mat.get_shader_parameter("corner_radius")), float(RADIUS)),
		"the shine mask matches the card's corner radius"
	)
	var measured: Vector2 = mat.get_shader_parameter("rect_size")
	_check(
		measured.is_equal_approx(CARD_SIZE),
		"the shader measures the card in pixels (%s)" % str(measured)
	)

	var uniforms: PackedStringArray = PackedStringArray()
	for uniform: Dictionary in mat.shader.get_shader_uniform_list():
		uniforms.append(String(uniform.get("name", "")))
	for required: String in ["rect_size", "corner_radius", "tint", "sheen"]:
		_check(uniforms.has(required), "the shader exposes `%s`" % required)

	await _discard(card)


func test_face_is_a_light_glass_wash_rimmed_with_the_accent() -> void:
	var card: Button = await _glossy_card(ACCENT)
	var normal: StyleBoxFlat = card.get_theme_stylebox("normal") as StyleBoxFlat
	var hover: StyleBoxFlat = card.get_theme_stylebox("hover") as StyleBoxFlat
	var pressed: StyleBoxFlat = card.get_theme_stylebox("pressed") as StyleBoxFlat
	_check(normal != null and hover != null and pressed != null, "the card paints all three states")
	if normal == null or hover == null or pressed == null:
		await _discard(card)
		return

	var body: Color = MenuTheme.gloss_body(ACCENT)
	_check(normal.bg_color == body, "the face is the glossy body for the accent")
	_check(
		body.a < 0.999,
		"the face is a little transparent, so the page reads through it (a=%.2f)" % body.a
	)
	_check(
		body.a >= 0.8,
		"the glass stays opaque enough for the dark ink over it (a=%.2f)" % body.a
	)
	_check(
		body.get_luminance() > 0.85,
		"the face stays light enough for the theme's dark ink (%.2f)" % body.get_luminance()
	)
	_check(
		normal.bg_color.r < 0.999 or normal.bg_color.b < 0.999,
		"the face is tinted, not dead white"
	)
	_check(
		normal.corner_radius_top_left == RADIUS and normal.corner_radius_bottom_right == RADIUS,
		"the face keeps the card's rounded corners"
	)
	_check(
		normal.border_width_left == DesignTokens.BORDER_SUBTLE,
		"the face is rimmed with a hairline"
	)
	_check(
		is_equal_approx(normal.border_color.a, 0.45),
		"the rim is a soft accent line, not the old solid accent"
	)

	# The gloss sits ON TOP of the elevation, so hover still lifts and a press
	# still sinks — the shine only adds light.
	_check(
		hover.bg_color.get_luminance() > normal.bg_color.get_luminance(),
		"hover lifts the face"
	)
	_check(
		hover.shadow_size >= normal.shadow_size,
		"hover keeps the deeper shadow"
	)
	_check(
		pressed.bg_color.get_luminance() < normal.bg_color.get_luminance(),
		"press sinks the face"
	)
	_check(
		is_equal_approx(hover.bg_color.a, body.a) and is_equal_approx(pressed.bg_color.a, body.a),
		"every state keeps the same glass, so it never firms up or clears"
	)
	_check(
		card.get_theme_stylebox("focus") == hover,
		"focus shows the same lifted face"
	)

	await _discard(card)


func test_the_coating_issues_a_draw_command_to_paint_on() -> void:
	# A material only applies to DRAW COMMANDS, and a bare Control issues none:
	# without its own `_draw()` the coating would sit in the tree, carry a shader
	# and still be invisible. That bug is silent, so it is pinned here.
	var card: Button = await _glossy_card(ACCENT)
	var gloss: GlossSheen = _glosses(card)[0]
	_check(
		gloss.has_method("_draw"),
		"the coating issues a draw command, so its shader actually runs"
	)

	# The sheen the tween animates is the same value the shader receives.
	gloss.sheen = 0.42
	var mat: ShaderMaterial = gloss.material as ShaderMaterial
	_check(
		is_equal_approx(float(mat.get_shader_parameter("sheen")), 0.42),
		"the shine state is pushed into the shader (%.2f)"
		% float(mat.get_shader_parameter("sheen"))
	)
	gloss.sheen = GlossSheenScript.SHEEN_REST

	await _discard(card)


func test_restyling_reuses_the_coating_instead_of_stacking_it() -> void:
	var card: Button = await _glossy_card(ACCENT)

	var mat: ShaderMaterial = gloss.material as ShaderMaterial

		(mat.get_shader_parameter("tint") as Color) == OTHER_ACCENT,

	_check(
		(card.get_theme_stylebox("normal") as StyleBoxFlat).bg_color

		"the face is repainted for the new accent"
	)
	_check(
		card.mouse_entered.get_connections().size() == 1,
		"the hover wiring is not attached twice"
	)

	await _discard(card)


func test_hover_brightens_the_shine_and_a_press_flattens_it() -> void:
	var card: Button = await _glossy_card(ACCENT)
	var gloss: GlossSheen = _glosses(card)[0]
	_check(is_equal_approx(gloss.sheen, GlossSheenScript.SHEEN_REST), "the shine rests at zero")

		await _wait_for_sheen(gloss, GlossSheenScript.SHEEN_HOVER),

	_check(
		await _wait_for_sheen(gloss, GlossSheenScript.SHEEN_PRESSED),
		"pressing flattens the shine (%.2f)" % gloss.sheen
	)

	card.button_up.emit()
	_check(
		await _wait_for_sheen(gloss, GlossSheenScript.SHEEN_REST),
		"releasing settles the shine back to rest (%.2f)" % gloss.sheen
	)

	await _discard(card)


func test_lesson_menu_section_cards_are_all_glossy() -> void:

## Renders a glossy button offscreen and reads the pixels back, so the shine is
## verified by what it actually paints and not only by its settings. Skipped when
## the run has no rendering driver (headless), where every pixel reads as zero.
func test_the_shine_paints_a_top_highlight_over_a_shaded_bottom() -> void:
	# The dummy renderer of a headless run has no texture to read back, so this
	# check only runs where something actually draws (the editor's Game tab,
	# `godot --path .` and so on).
	if DisplayServer.get_name() == "headless":
		print("SKIP  headless run — the pixel check needs a rendering driver")
		return

	var size := Vector2i(400, 220)
	var viewport := SubViewport.new()
	viewport.size = size
	viewport.transparent_bg = true
	viewport.render_target_update_mode = SubViewport.UPDATE_ALWAYS
	add_child(viewport)

	var card := Button.new()
	card.text = ""
	card.position = Vector2.ZERO
	card.size = Vector2(size)
	viewport.add_child(card)
	MenuStyle.style_gloss_card(card, ACCENT, RADIUS)
	await _frames(2)
	await _wait_for_draw()

	var img: Image = viewport.get_texture().get_image()
	if img == null or img.get_width() == 0 or _is_blank(img):
		print("SKIP  no rendering driver in this run — pixel check needs a window")
		viewport.queue_free()
		return

	var corner: Color = img.get_pixel(3, 3)
	var top: Color = img.get_pixel(size.x / 2, 24)
	var middle: Color = img.get_pixel(size.x / 2, size.y / 2)
	var bottom: Color = img.get_pixel(size.x / 2, size.y - 12)

	print(
		"gloss pixels — corner a=%.2f  top=%.3f  middle=%.3f  bottom=%.3f"
		% [corner.a, top.get_luminance(), middle.get_luminance(), bottom.get_luminance()]
	)
	_print_luminance_map(img)

	_check(corner.a < 0.5, "the shine keeps the rounded corner cut (a=%.2f)" % corner.a)
	# The glass is see-through: with nothing behind it, the face pixel keeps the
	# leftover transparency instead of reading as a solid slab.
	_check(
		middle.a < 0.99,
		"the face is a little transparent, so the page behind it shows (a=%.2f)" % middle.a
	)
	_check(
		middle.a > 0.7,
		"the glass stays solid enough to carry the ink over the artwork (a=%.2f)" % middle.a
	)
	_check(
		top.get_luminance() > middle.get_luminance(),
		"the top of the card is brighter than its middle (%.3f > %.3f)"
		% [top.get_luminance(), middle.get_luminance()]
	)
	_check(
		middle.get_luminance() > bottom.get_luminance(),
		"the bottom of the card is shaded under the shine (%.3f > %.3f)"
		% [middle.get_luminance(), bottom.get_luminance()]
	)
	_check(
		middle.b > middle.r,
		"the face carries the accent's hue (b=%.3f > r=%.3f)" % [middle.b, middle.r]
	)

	viewport.queue_free()


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- helpers --

## A real menu card, sized like a section card and dressed glossy.
func _glossy_card(accent_col: Color) -> Button:
	var card: Button = MenuStyle.make_card("Section", "زیربخش", "📘", accent_col, int(CARD_SIZE.y))
	card.size = CARD_SIZE
	add_child(card)
	await _frames(2)
	MenuStyle.style_gloss_card(card, accent_col, RADIUS)
	await _frames(2)
	return card


func _glosses(node: Node) -> Array[GlossSheen]:
	var out: Array[GlossSheen] = []
	for child: Node in node.get_children():
		if child is GlossSheen:
			out.append(child as GlossSheen)
	return out


## Waits (bounded) for the shine tween to reach `target`, so the assertion does
## not depend on the frame rate of the test run.
func _wait_for_sheen(gloss: GlossSheen, target: float, tolerance: float = 0.02) -> bool:
	var deadline: int = Time.get_ticks_msec() + 2000
	while Time.get_ticks_msec() < deadline:
		await get_tree().process_frame
		if absf(gloss.sheen - target) <= tolerance:
			return true
	return absf(gloss.sheen - target) <= tolerance


func _frames(count: int) -> void:
	for _i: int in range(count):
		await get_tree().process_frame


## Waits for one real draw, but never blocks the suite: a headless run may never
## emit frame_post_draw, so the wait falls back to a plain frame budget.
func _wait_for_draw() -> void:
	var drawn := [false]
	var on_draw := func() -> void: drawn[0] = true
	RenderingServer.frame_post_draw.connect(on_draw)
	for _i: int in range(6):
		await get_tree().process_frame
		if drawn[0]:
			break
	RenderingServer.frame_post_draw.disconnect(on_draw)


func _discard(node: Node) -> void:
	node.queue_free()
	await get_tree().process_frame


func _is_blank(img: Image) -> bool:
	for y: int in range(0, img.get_height(), 8):
		for x: int in range(0, img.get_width(), 8):
			if img.get_pixel(x, y).a > 0.0:
				return false
	return true


## Coarse ASCII luminance map — makes the render's look readable in the test log
## (0 = black, 9 = white, "." = transparent).
func _print_luminance_map(img: Image) -> void:
	var cols := 40
	var rows := 11
	var step_x := maxi(1, img.get_width() / cols)
	var step_y := maxi(1, img.get_height() / rows)
	for row: int in range(rows):
		var line := ""
		for col: int in range(cols):
			var px: Color = img.get_pixel(
				mini(col * step_x + step_x / 2, img.get_width() - 1),
				mini(row * step_y + step_y / 2, img.get_height() - 1)
			)
			if px.a < 0.5:
				line += "."
			else:
				line += str(clampi(int(px.get_luminance() * 10.0), 0, 9))
		print("      " + line)


func _check(condition: bool, label: String) -> void:
	assert(condition, label)
	print("PASS  " + label)
```

```gdscript
func test_no_screen_keeps_the_old_dead_band() -> void:
	# The bar shrank by 120 px, so a screen still positioning its content where
	# the old 320 px bar ended would show an empty band under the new one.
	var offenders: Array[String] = []
	for path: String in _header_scene_paths():
		var inside_header := false
		for line: String in FileAccess.get_file_as_string(path).split("\n"):
			var trimmed := line.strip_edges()
			if trimmed.begins_with("[node "):
				inside_header = trimmed.contains("name=\"HeaderBar\"")
				continue
			if inside_header or not trimmed.begins_with("offset_top = "):
				continue
			var value := trimmed.trim_prefix("offset_top = ").to_float()
			if value >= 300.0 and value < 600.0:
				offenders.append("%s (%.0f px)" % [path.get_file(), value])
	_check(offenders.is_empty(), "no screen starts its content in the old dead band %s" % str(offenders))

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
#  FIXTURES
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

## Builds a header the way the .tscn screens author it: a 320 px panel with a
## row of text buttons, so the test proves the engine re-shapes it. The bar is
## parented straight to the test node, so freeing it frees the whole fixture.
func _spawn_header(bar_name: String, with_margin: bool, full: bool, omit: Array = []) -> PanelContainer:
	var bar := PanelContainer.new()
	bar.name = bar_name
	bar.set_anchors_preset(Control.PRESET_TOP_WIDE)
	bar.offset_bottom = 320.0
	add_child(bar)

	var row := HBoxContainer.new()
	row.name = "HeaderContent"
	row.size_flags_horizontal = Control.SIZE_SHRINK_CENTER
	row.add_theme_constant_override("separation", 45)
	if with_margin:
		var margin := MarginContainer.new()
		margin.name = "MarginContainer"
		bar.add_child(margin)
		margin.add_child(row)
	else:
		bar.add_child(row)

	var back := Button.new()
	back.name = "BackButton"
	back.text = "بازگشت"
	row.add_child(back)

	if not full:
		var counter := Label.new()
		counter.name = "DueCounter"
		counter.text = "۱۲ کلمه"
		row.add_child(counter)
		return bar

	if not omit.has("HomeButton"):
		var home := Button.new()
		home.name = "HomeButton"
		home.text = "🏠"
		row.add_child(home)

	var title := Label.new()
	title.name = "HeaderTitle"
	title.text = "درس ۱\nمکالمه"
	var settings := LabelSettings.new()
	settings.font_size = 55
	title.label_settings = settings
	row.add_child(title)

	if not omit.has("TranslationToggleButton"):
		var translation := Button.new()
		translation.name = "TranslationToggleButton"
		translation.text = "Translate"
		row.add_child(translation)
	if not omit.has("AudioButton"):
		var audio := Button.new()
		audio.name = "AudioButton"
		audio.text = "صدا"
		row.add_child(audio)
	if not omit.has("LeitnerButton"):
		var leitner := Button.new()
		leitner.name = "LeitnerButton"
		row.add_child(leitner)
	return bar


## A lighter screen: only a back arrow, the title and the audio button.
func _spawn_light_header(bar_name: String) -> PanelContainer:
	return await _spawn_header(
		bar_name, false, true, ["HomeButton", "TranslationToggleButton", "LeitnerButton"]
	)


func _buttons(root: Node) -> Array[Button]:
	var out: Array[Button] = []
	var stack: Array[Node] = [root]
	while not stack.is_empty():
		var node: Node = stack.pop_back()
		if node is Button:
			out.append(node as Button)
			continue
		for child: Node in node.get_children():
			stack.push_back(child)
	return out


func _header_scene_paths() -> Array[String]:
	var out: Array[String] = []
	var stack: Array[String] = ["res://scenes"]
	while not stack.is_empty():
		var dir_path: String = stack.pop_back()
		var dir := DirAccess.open(dir_path)
		if dir == null:
			continue
		for sub: String in dir.get_directories():
			stack.append(dir_path.path_join(sub))
		for file_name: String in dir.get_files():
			if not file_name.ends_with(".tscn"):
				continue
			var path := dir_path.path_join(file_name)
			if FileAccess.get_file_as_string(path).contains("name=\"HeaderBar\""):
				out.append(path)
	out.sort()
	return out


## Height a scene authors for its HeaderBar: `offset_bottom` on an anchored
## bar, or `custom_minimum_size = Vector2(0, N)` on the main menu's Control.
func _authored_header_height(text: String) -> float:
	var inside := false
	var found := -1.0
	for line: String in text.split("\n"):
		var trimmed := line.strip_edges()
		if trimmed.begins_with("[node "):
			inside = trimmed.contains("name=\"HeaderBar\"")
			continue
		if not inside:
			continue
		if trimmed.begins_with("offset_bottom = "):
			found = maxf(found, trimmed.trim_prefix("offset_bottom = ").to_float())
		elif trimmed.begins_with("custom_minimum_size = Vector2("):
			var pair := trimmed.trim_prefix("custom_minimum_size = Vector2(").split(")")
			if pair.size() > 0:
				var parts := String(pair[0]).split(",")
				if parts.size() == 2:
					found = maxf(found, String(parts[1]).strip_edges().to_float())
	return found


func _screen_size() -> Vector2:
	return get_viewport().get_visible_rect().size


func _check(condition: bool, label: String) -> void:
	assert(condition, label)
	print("PASS  " + label)
```

## File: `res://tests/test_native_drag.gd`

```gdscript
extends Control
## ============================================================
##  NATIVE DRAG INTEGRATION TEST — «بازی املا»'s drag, as the ENGINE runs it.
##
##  The unit suite (scenes/word_game/scrambled/test_scrambled_words.gd) calls
##  the drag methods directly. This one goes a level up and feeds real press,
##  motion and release events through the Viewport, so the parts of a drag that
##  only the engine can get wrong are exercised for real:
##    * deciding which Control may start a drag at all,
##    * asking it for its payload — and building the carried preview,
##    * resolving the drop target by walking the tree, which is exactly where a
##      MOUSE_FILTER_STOP tile that refused a drop would break the board,
##    * reporting NOTIFICATION_DRAG_END, so the letter can be picked up again.
##
##  WHAT IT DOES NOT ASSERT: where the letter lands. The engine resolves a drop
##  from the *real* pointer rather than from a synthesized event, so a harness
##  cannot steer the landing slot — `_can_drop_data`/`_drop_data` are handed the
##  live cursor's position whatever the events say. Which slot a drop opens and
##  lands in is covered by test_scrambled_words.gd, which passes those positions
##  in itself.
##
##  Run it with run_scene on res://tests/TestNativeDrag.tscn.
## ============================================================

const BOARD_SCENE := preload("res://scenes/word_game/scrambled/TileBoard.tscn")

## One motion step. The engine accumulates each event's `relative` and only
## agrees a gesture is a drag — rather than a click — once it has travelled
## far enough, so a single frame-jump motion would not do.
const STEP := 24.0
## How far right the letter is carried: past two slots, as in the unit test.
const CARRY := 700.0

var _failures := 0
var _board: ScrambledTileBoard = null
var _settled: Array = []


func _ready() -> void:
	# The harness must never answer for the board: with IGNORE the drop search
	# walks straight past it to whatever the crosshair is really over.
	mouse_filter = Control.MOUSE_FILTER_IGNORE
	set_anchors_preset(Control.PRESET_FULL_RECT)
	await _run()


func _run() -> void:
	var controller := ScrambledWordController.new()
	controller.setup({"word": "sun"}, 987654)
	_board = BOARD_SCENE.instantiate() as ScrambledTileBoard
	# Placed by hand so the scripted finger has known ground to work on. The
	# board measures its own row, so nothing here depends on the window size —
	# but its scene ships stretched, and a stretched Control has its size
	# re-imposed by every layout pass, so the anchors go back to top-left first.
	_board.set_anchors_preset(Control.PRESET_TOP_LEFT)
	_board.position = Vector2(200.0, 400.0)
	_board.size = Vector2(1000.0, 400.0)
	_board.arrangement_settled.connect(func(solved: bool) -> void: _settled.append(solved))
	add_child(_board)
	await get_tree().process_frame
	await get_tree().process_frame
	_board.build(controller, false)
	# The letters fly to their slots; a player drags after they have landed, so
	# the scripted finger waits for the row to be at rest too.
	await get_tree().create_timer(0.4).timeout

	_check(_board.tile_count() == 3, "the board dealt three letters")

	var first: ScrambledTile = _board.get_child(0)
	var from := first.get_global_rect().get_center()
	var to := from + Vector2(CARRY, 0.0)

	# --- a real press-and-travel, straight into the Viewport -----------------
	await _drag_start(from)
	_check(first.state == ScrambledTile.State.DRAGGING,
		"the engine started a native drag on the pressed letter")
	_check(_board.is_busy(), "the board opened a slot for the letter")
	# Rule 2's preview: the player must be handed something to carry. It lives
	# in the Viewport's own drag layer, so it is looked for there.
	_check(_drag_preview() != null, "the engine is holding a carried copy for the finger")

	await _drag_move_to(from, to)
	await _release(to)
	await get_tree().create_timer(0.6).timeout

	_check(not _board.is_busy(), "the drag ends with nothing carried")
	_check(not _settled.is_empty(), "the row settled and was judged")
	_check(is_equal_approx(first.modulate.a, 1.0),
		"the carried copy is solid again (alpha %.2f)" % first.modulate.a)

	print("---")
	print("ALL TESTS PASSED" if _failures == 0 else "%d TEST(S) FAILED" % _failures)


############################################################
# THE SCRIPTED GESTURE
############################################################
## Press, then enough travel for the engine to call it a drag.
func _drag_start(from: Vector2) -> void:
	_send_button(from, true)
	await get_tree().process_frame
	for i in 2:
		var to := from + Vector2(STEP * float(i + 1), 0.0)
		_send_motion(to, Vector2(STEP, 0.0))
		await get_tree().process_frame


## The rest of the travel: this is where the engine re-resolves the drop target
## under the finger and tells it the letter is hovering over it.
func _drag_move_to(from: Vector2, to: Vector2) -> void:
	var here := from + Vector2(STEP * 2.0, 0.0)
	_send_motion(to, to - here)
	await get_tree().process_frame


## The finger lifting: the engine resolves the target one last time and
## delivers the drop to it.
func _release(to: Vector2) -> void:
	_send_button(to, false)
	await get_tree().process_frame


func _send_button(point: Vector2, pressed: bool) -> void:
	var event := InputEventMouseButton.new()
	event.button_index = MOUSE_BUTTON_LEFT
	event.pressed = pressed
	event.position = point
	event.global_position = point
	# The drag machinery reads the button mask, so a held button has to say so.
	event.button_mask = MOUSE_BUTTON_MASK_LEFT if pressed else 0
	# `true`: the coordinates this harness builds come from get_global_rect(),
	# which is the Viewport's own space — the space the GUI is hit-tested in.
	get_viewport().push_input(event, true)


## `relative` carries the delta: the engine accumulates it to tell a drag from
## a click, so a motion with a zero delta would keep the drag from starting.
func _send_motion(point: Vector2, delta: Vector2) -> void:
	var event := InputEventMouseMotion.new()
	event.position = point
	event.global_position = point
	event.relative = delta
	event.button_mask = MOUSE_BUTTON_MASK_LEFT
	get_viewport().push_input(event, true)


## The carried copy the engine holds during a drag lives in the Viewport's own
## internal drag layer, so the only honest way to check that the player really
## was handed something is to look for it there.
func _drag_preview() -> TilePreview:
	for child in get_viewport().get_children(true):
		for grandchild in child.get_children(true):
			if grandchild is TilePreview:
				return grandchild as TilePreview
	return null


func _check(condition: bool, label: String) -> void:
	if not condition:
		_failures += 1
	print(("PASS  " if condition else "FAIL  ") + label)
```

```gdscript
class_name SafeAreaInsetTests

const SAFE_AREA_SCRIPT: Script = preload("res://autoload/SafeAreaInset.gd")


func test_scene_content_keeps_its_configured_top_layout() -> void:
	var scene_root: Control = Control.new()
	scene_root.set_anchors_preset(Control.PRESET_FULL_RECT)
	var background: ColorRect = ColorRect.new()
	background.set_anchors_preset(Control.PRESET_FULL_RECT)
	var content: Control = Control.new()
	content.set_anchors_preset(Control.PRESET_FULL_RECT)
	scene_root.add_child(background)
	scene_root.add_child(content)
	add_child(scene_root)
	await get_tree().process_frame

	SAFE_AREA_SCRIPT.apply_to_scene(scene_root)
	_check(is_zero_approx(content.offset_top), "Full-screen scene content keeps its configured top edge")
	_check(is_zero_approx(content.offset_bottom), "Full-screen scene content keeps its configured bottom edge")
	_check(is_zero_approx(background.offset_top), "Background remains full-screen without an added top adjustment")

	scene_root.queue_free()
	await get_tree().process_frame


func _check(condition: bool, label: String) -> void:
	assert(condition, label)
	print("PASS  " + label)
```

## File: `res://tests/test_scene_theming.gd`

```gdscript
extends Node
## ============================================================
##  SCENE THEMING SWEEP — run with run_scene on TestSceneTheming.tscn.
##
##  Proves the claim the redesign rests on: every scene in the app still
##  loads, instantiates, enters the tree and survives the app-wide styling
##  pass. Because the entire restyle is delivered through the Theme resource
##  and ThemeService's scene walk — not by editing scenes — this is the test
##  that shows "all 49 scenes" really were restyled rather than assumed.
##
##  Scenes named *Test* are skipped: they are not app screens, and several of
##  them run their own suites on _ready.
##
##  EXIT-TIME NOTE: this sweep deliberately boots all 47 screens, which
##  populates process-lifetime caches — most visibly MenuStyle._font_cache, a
##  `static var` holding every font the app loads. Godot therefore reports
##  resources "still in use at exit" after a sweep run (1 normally, 2 with
##  application/run/low_processor_mode enabled, which parks one more canvas
##  resource until the harness force-quits). Both counts are teardown
##  accounting in a dying process, not leaks from this test: every scene
##  instance is freed here, and a plain app launch + quit (verified with
##  --verbose --quit-after) exits with ZERO such reports either way.
## ============================================================

const SCENE_ROOT := "res://scenes"

var _failures := 0


func test_all_app_scenes_theme_cleanly() -> void:
	await _sweep()
	_report()


func _sweep() -> void:
	var paths := _collect_scenes(SCENE_ROOT)
	paths.sort()
	_check(paths.size() >= 40, "the sweep found the app's scenes (%d)" % paths.size())

	var themed := 0
	var failures: Array = []
	for path in paths:
		var packed := load(path)
		if packed == null or not (packed is PackedScene):
			failures.append("%s (not a PackedScene)" % path)
			continue
		var instance: Node = (packed as PackedScene).instantiate()
		if instance == null:
			failures.append("%s (instantiate returned null)" % path)
			continue

		# Enter the tree so any _ready-time work runs for real, then run the
		# same styling pass the app runs on every scene change.
		add_child(instance)
		Global.style_scene(instance)
		await get_tree().process_frame
		themed += 1
		remove_child(instance)
		instance.free()

	_check(failures.is_empty(),
		"every scene instantiates, enters the tree and survives styling (%d/%d ok; failed: %s)"
			% [themed, paths.size(), str(failures)])


## Recursively collects every .tscn under `dir`, skipping test scenes.
func _collect_scenes(dir: String) -> Array:
	var out: Array = []
	var handle := DirAccess.open(dir)
	if handle == null:
		return out
	handle.list_dir_begin()
	var entry := handle.get_next()
	while entry != "":
		if entry.begins_with("."):
			entry = handle.get_next()
			continue
		var full := dir.path_join(entry)
		if handle.current_is_dir():
			out.append_array(_collect_scenes(full))
		elif entry.ends_with(".tscn") and not entry.to_lower().contains("test"):
			out.append(full)
		entry = handle.get_next()
	handle.list_dir_end()
	return out


func _check(condition: bool, label: String) -> void:
	if not condition:
		_failures += 1
	print(("PASS  " if condition else "FAIL  ") + label)


func _report() -> void:
	print("---")
	print("ALL TESTS PASSED" if _failures == 0 else "%d TEST(S) FAILED" % _failures)
```

## File: `res://tests/test_scrambled_words.gd`

```gdscript
extends Node
## ============================================================
##  SCRAMBLED WORDS TESTS — run with run_scene on TestScrambledWords.tscn.
##
##  Covers the pure game modules: the word bank, the deterministic daily
##  picker, the scramble/solve rules, the score table and both records
##  (daily competition + practice), plus the session state machine and the
##  drag-and-drop board. The UI screens themselves are exercised by running
##  ScrambledWords.tscn, which needs the real autoloads.
##
##  The daily and practice records write to user://, so the runner parks the
##  player's real file first and puts it back afterwards: running the tests
##  must never eat a recorded score.
## ============================================================

const SAVE_PATH := "user://scrambled_words.json"

var _failures := 0
var _parked := ""


func _ready() -> void:
	_park_user_file()

	test_bank()
	test_daily_picker()
	test_scramble()
	test_score_table()
	test_daily_record()
	test_practice_record()
	test_learning_session()
	test_competition_session()

	await test_board_first_word_layout()
	await test_gameplay_first_word_visible()
	await test_gameplay_layout()
	await test_gameplay_theme_variations()
	await test_board_drag()
	await test_tile_drag_payload()
	await test_board_drag_cancel()

	_restore_user_file()

	print("---")
	print("ALL TESTS PASSED" if _failures == 0 else "%d TEST(S) FAILED" % _failures)


############################################################
# user:// HOUSEKEEPING
############################################################
func _park_user_file() -> void:
	_parked = "" if not FileAccess.file_exists(SAVE_PATH) else FileAccess.get_file_as_string(SAVE_PATH)
	_remove_save()


func _restore_user_file() -> void:
	_remove_save()
	if not _parked.is_empty():
		var file := FileAccess.open(SAVE_PATH, FileAccess.WRITE)
		if file != null:
			file.store_string(_parked)
			file.close()
	ScrambledScoreManager.reset_cache()


func _remove_save() -> void:
	if FileAccess.file_exists(SAVE_PATH):
		DirAccess.remove_absolute(SAVE_PATH)


############################################################
# WORD BANK
############################################################
func test_bank() -> void:
	ScrambledData.reset_cache()
	_check(ScrambledData.book_count() >= 3, "the bank has at least three books (%d)" % ScrambledData.book_count())
	_check(ScrambledData.has_book(1) and ScrambledData.has_lesson(1, 2), "Vision 1 / Lesson 2 exists")
	_check(ScrambledData.word_count(1, 2) >= 10,
		"Vision 1 / Lesson 2 is playable (%d words)" % ScrambledData.word_count(1, 2))
	_check(not ScrambledData.lesson_title_fa(1, 2).is_empty(), "the lesson carries its Persian title")

	var expected := 0
	var letters_ok := true
	var meanings_ok := true
	for book_data in ScrambledData.books():
		for lesson_data in book_data["lessons"]:
			expected += int(lesson_data["word_count"])
			var seen := {}
			for entry in lesson_data["words"]:
				var spelling := str(entry["word"])
				if spelling.length() < 3 or spelling.length() > 12:
					letters_ok = false
				for ch in spelling:
					var lower := ch.to_lower()
					if lower < "a" or lower > "z":
						letters_ok = false
				if str(entry["meaning"]).is_empty():
					meanings_ok = false
				var key := spelling.to_lower()
				if seen.has(key):
					letters_ok = false
				seen[key] = true
	_check(letters_ok, "every word is 3-12 latin letters and unique inside its lesson")
	_check(meanings_ok, "every word carries an English meaning")
	_check(ScrambledData.all_words().size() == expected,
		"the flat bank matches the lesson totals (%d words)" % expected)
	var ordered := ScrambledData.words_ordered(1, 2)
	_check(ordered.size() == ScrambledData.word_count(1, 2), "ordering a lesson keeps every word")
	var ramp_ok := true
	for i in range(1, ordered.size()):
		if str(ordered[i]["word"]).length() < str(ordered[i - 1]["word"]).length():
			ramp_ok = false
	_check(ramp_ok, "learning deals the shortest words first")


############################################################
# DAILY PICKER
############################################################
func test_daily_picker() -> void:
	ScrambledDailyPicker.reset_cache()
	_check(ScrambledDailyPicker.pick().size() == ScrambledDailyPicker.WORDS_PER_DAY,
		"today's challenge deals five words (%d)" % ScrambledDailyPicker.pick().size())

	var first := _word_list(ScrambledDailyPicker.pick_for_day(1000))
	_check(first == _word_list(ScrambledDailyPicker.pick_for_day(1000)),
		"the same day always deals the same words")
	_check(first != _word_list(ScrambledDailyPicker.pick_for_day(1001)),
		"the next day deals a different set")

	var overlap := false
	for word in _word_list(ScrambledDailyPicker.pick_for_day(1001)):
		if first.has(word):
			overlap = true
	_check(not overlap, "consecutive days never share a word")

	var bank := _word_list(ScrambledData.all_words())
	var in_bank := true
	for word in first:
		if not bank.has(word):
			in_bank = false
	_check(in_bank, "every daily word comes from the bank")
	_check(_word_list(ScrambledDailyPicker.pick()) == _word_list(
		ScrambledDailyPicker.pick_for_day(ScrambledDailyPicker.day_index())),
		"pick() is today's window of the frozen order")
	_check(ScrambledDailyPicker.puzzle_id().begins_with("scrambled-"),
		"the puzzle id carries the date (%s)" % ScrambledDailyPicker.puzzle_id())
	_check(not ScrambledDailyPicker.time_left_text().is_empty(),
		"the countdown reads (%s)" % ScrambledDailyPicker.time_left_text())
	var left := ScrambledDailyPicker.seconds_until_next_day()
	_check(left > 0 and left <= ScrambledDailyPicker.SECONDS_PER_DAY, "the countdown stays inside one day")
############################################################
# SCRAMBLE / SOLVE RULES
############################################################
func test_scramble() -> void:
	var data := {"word": "planet", "meaning": "A world", "meaning_fa": "سیاره"}
	var a := ScrambledWordController.new()
	a.setup(data, 4242)
	_check(a.letter_count() == 6, "the controller keeps every letter")
	_check(ScrambledWordController.letters_to_text(a.letters) != "PLANET",
		"a seeded scramble is never already solved (%s)" % ScrambledWordController.letters_to_text(a.letters))

	var b := ScrambledWordController.new()
	b.setup(data, 4242)
	_check(ScrambledWordController.letters_to_text(a.letters) == ScrambledWordController.letters_to_text(b.letters),
		"the same seed deals the same scramble")

	var c := ScrambledWordController.new()
	c.setup(data, 99)
	_check(ScrambledWordController.letters_to_text(c.letters) != ScrambledWordController.letters_to_text(a.letters),
		"a different seed deals a different scramble")

	_check(a.is_solved(["P", "L", "A", "N", "E", "T"]), "the answer spells the word")
	_check(not a.is_solved(["P", "L", "A", "N", "E", "E"]), "a wrong letter does not")
	_check(not a.is_solved(["P", "L", "A", "N", "E"]), "a short board does not")

	_check(a.misplaced(["P", "L", "A", "N", "E", "T"]).is_empty(), "a solved board has no misplaced letter")
	_check(a.misplaced(["P", "L", "A", "N", "T", "E"]) == [4, 5], "the last two letters are reported misplaced")
	_check(a.is_near_miss(["P", "L", "A", "N", "T", "E"]), "two wrong letters is a near miss")
	_check(not a.is_near_miss(["T", "E", "N", "A", "L", "P"]), "a scrambled board is not a near miss")

	# A word whose letters are all the same cannot be scrambled.
	var same := ScrambledWordController.new()
	same.setup({"word": "mmm"}, 7)
	_check(ScrambledWordController.letters_to_text(same.letters) == "MMM",
		"an unscramblable word keeps its order instead of looping forever")


############################################################
# SCORE TABLE
############################################################
func test_score_table() -> void:
	_check(ScrambledScoreManager.points_for(5.0, false) == 100, "under 10s is worth 100")
	_check(ScrambledScoreManager.points_for(10.0, false) == 100, "exactly 10s is still 100")
	_check(ScrambledScoreManager.points_for(10.1, false) == 60, "past 10s is worth 60")
	_check(ScrambledScoreManager.points_for(30.0, false) == 60, "exactly 30s is still 60")
	_check(ScrambledScoreManager.points_for(30.1, false) == 40, "past 30s is worth 40")
	_check(ScrambledScoreManager.points_for(50.0, false) == 40, "exactly 50s is still 40")
	_check(ScrambledScoreManager.points_for(50.1, false) == 30, "past 50s is worth 30")
	_check(ScrambledScoreManager.points_for(60.0, false) == 30, "exactly 60s is still 30")
	_check(ScrambledScoreManager.points_for(120.0, false) == 20, "a slow solve is worth 20")

	_check(ScrambledScoreManager.points_for(5.0, true) == 50, "a hint halves the top score")
	_check(ScrambledScoreManager.points_for(20.0, true) == 30, "a hint halves the middle score")
	_check(ScrambledScoreManager.points_for(120.0, true) == 10, "a hinted slow solve is floored at 10")
	_check(ScrambledScoreManager.points_for(120.0, true) == ScrambledScoreManager.MIN_WORD_POINTS,
		"the penalty never drops a word below the floor")

	_check(ScrambledScoreManager.MAX_DAILY_SCORE == 500, "a perfect day is 500")
	_check(ScrambledScoreManager.MIN_DAILY_SCORE == 50, "the floor of a five-word day is 50")
	_check(str(ScrambledScoreManager.rating_for(500)["label"]) == "شگفت‌انگیز!", "500 rates top")
	_check(str(ScrambledScoreManager.rating_for(50)["label"]) == "دوباره تلاش کن", "50 rates bottom")
	_check(int(ScrambledScoreManager.rating_for(300)["min_score"]) == 250, "300 falls in the third band")


############################################################
# RECORDS
############################################################
func test_daily_record() -> void:
	ScrambledScoreManager.reset_cache()
	_remove_save()
	_check(ScrambledScoreManager.today_score() == 0, "a fresh record starts at zero")
	_check(ScrambledScoreManager.played_days() == 0, "no day is played yet")
	_check(not ScrambledScoreManager.today_played(), "today is not played yet")

	_check(ScrambledScoreManager.save_daily_attempt(320, 5, 1, 41.5), "the first attempt sets the day's best")
	_check(ScrambledScoreManager.today_score() == 320, "the day keeps its score")
	_check(ScrambledScoreManager.today_attempts() == 1, "the attempt is counted")
	_check(ScrambledScoreManager.played_days() == 1, "the day is counted once")
	_check(ScrambledGameManager.start_competition() == false, "a second daily challenge start is rejected")
	_check(not ScrambledScoreManager.save_daily_attempt(120, 5, 3, 90.0),
		"duplicate result record does not improve the daily best")
	_check(ScrambledScoreManager.today_score() == 320, "the best score remains unchanged")
	_check(ScrambledScoreManager.today_attempts() == 2, "direct record calls still count attempts")

	_check(ScrambledScoreManager.save_daily_attempt(460, 5, 0, 33.0), "a higher direct record improves the best")
	_check(ScrambledScoreManager.today_score() == 460, "the day's best is updated")
	_check(ScrambledScoreManager.best_score() == 460, "the overall best follows")
	_check(ScrambledScoreManager.best_score_date() == ScrambledDailyPicker.date_key(), "the best date is today")
	_check(ScrambledScoreManager.total_attempts() == 3, "all record entries are counted")
	_check(ScrambledScoreManager.daily_history().size() == 1, "the history holds the played day")

	ScrambledScoreManager.reset_cache()
	_check(ScrambledScoreManager.today_score() == 460, "the record is read back from disk")
	_check(ScrambledScoreManager.played_days() == 1, "the played days survive a reload")

	# A corrupt file must never break a screen.
	var file := FileAccess.open(SAVE_PATH, FileAccess.WRITE)
	if file != null:
		file.store_string("{ this is not json")
		file.close()
	ScrambledScoreManager.reset_cache()
	_check(ScrambledScoreManager.today_score() == 0, "a corrupt record starts fresh")
	_check(ScrambledScoreManager.today_attempts() == 0, "a corrupt record keeps no attempts")


func test_practice_record() -> void:
	ScrambledScoreManager.reset_cache()
	_remove_save()
	var empty := ScrambledScoreManager.practice_stats(1, 2)
	_check(int(empty["words"]) == 0 and int(empty["plays"]) == 0, "an unpractised lesson reports zeros")

	ScrambledScoreManager.record_practice_word(1, 2, false, 12.0)
	ScrambledScoreManager.record_practice_word(1, 2, true, 30.5)
	ScrambledScoreManager.record_practice_word(1, 3, false, 8.0)
	var stats := ScrambledScoreManager.practice_stats(1, 2)
	_check(int(stats["words"]) == 2, "both words are recorded")
	_check(int(stats["hints"]) == 1, "the hinted word is counted")
	_check(is_equal_approx(float(stats["seconds"]), 42.5), "the time adds up (%s)" % str(stats["seconds"]))
	_check(ScrambledScoreManager.total_practice_words() == 3, "practice words add up across lessons")
	_check(int(ScrambledScoreManager.practice_stats(2, 1)["words"]) == 0, "another book stays untouched")

	ScrambledScoreManager.reset_cache()
	_check(int(ScrambledScoreManager.practice_stats(1, 2)["words"]) == 2, "practice survives a reload")
	_check(ScrambledScoreManager.practice_key(1, 2) == "1_2", "the practice key names the lesson")


############################################################
# SESSIONS
############################################################
func test_learning_session() -> void:
	ScrambledScoreManager.reset_cache()
	_remove_save()
	ScrambledGameManager.reset()
	ScrambledGameManager.reset_play_counts()

	_check(ScrambledGameManager.start_learning(1, 2), "learning mode deals Vision 1 / Lesson 2")
	_check(ScrambledGameManager.mode == ScrambledGameManager.Mode.LEARNING, "the mode is learning")
	_check(ScrambledGameManager.word_count() == ScrambledData.word_count(1, 2), "the whole lesson is dealt")
	_check(ScrambledGameManager.word_position() == 1, "the session starts on the first word")
	_check(ScrambledGameManager.hint_delay() == ScrambledGameManager.LEARNING_HINT_DELAY,
		"learning offers the hint after 30s")
	_check(ScrambledGameManager.controller != null, "the first word has a controller")
	_check(not ScrambledGameManager.controller.letters.is_empty(), "the board is dealt letters")
	_check(ScrambledGameManager.current_word_potential_points() == 0, "learning mode scores nothing")

	var first_word := ScrambledGameManager.controller.word
	var entry := ScrambledGameManager.solve_current_word()
	_check(str(entry.get("word", "")) == first_word, "the solved word is recorded")
	_check(ScrambledGameManager.correct_count() == 1, "one word is spelled")
	_check(int(ScrambledScoreManager.practice_stats(1, 2)["words"]) == 1,
		"learning practice is written word by word")
	_check(ScrambledGameManager.solve_current_word().is_empty(), "a solved word cannot be solved twice")

	_check(ScrambledGameManager.advance(), "the session moves to the second word")
	_check(ScrambledGameManager.state == ScrambledGameManager.State.PLAYING, "the new word is playable")
	_check(ScrambledGameManager.current_word_hint_used() == false, "the hint flag resets per word")
	ScrambledGameManager.mark_hint_used()
	_check(ScrambledGameManager.current_word_hint_used(), "the hint flag is remembered")

	var guard := 0
	while ScrambledGameManager.state != ScrambledGameManager.State.FINISHED and guard < 500:
		ScrambledGameManager.solve_current_word()
		ScrambledGameManager.advance()
		guard += 1
	_check(ScrambledGameManager.state == ScrambledGameManager.State.FINISHED, "the lesson ends on its last word")
	_check(ScrambledGameManager.correct_count() == ScrambledData.word_count(1, 2),
		"every word of the lesson was spelled (%d)" % ScrambledGameManager.correct_count())
	_check(ScrambledGameManager.hints_used() == 1, "the hint is counted once")
	_check(int(ScrambledScoreManager.practice_stats(1, 2)["words"]) == ScrambledData.word_count(1, 2),
		"the practice record ends with the whole lesson")
	_check(ScrambledGameManager.average_seconds() >= 0.0, "the session reports an average time")


func test_competition_session() -> void:
	ScrambledScoreManager.reset_cache()
	_remove_save()
	ScrambledGameManager.reset()

	_check(ScrambledGameManager.start_competition(), "competition mode deals today's words")
	_check(ScrambledGameManager.mode == ScrambledGameManager.Mode.COMPETITION, "the mode is competition")
	_check(ScrambledGameManager.word_count() == ScrambledDailyPicker.WORDS_PER_DAY, "five words are dealt")
	_check(ScrambledGameManager.hint_delay() == ScrambledGameManager.COMPETITION_HINT_DELAY,
		"competition offers the hint after 60s")
	_check(ScrambledGameManager.current_word_potential_points() == 100, "a fresh word is worth the top band")
	_check(ScrambledGameManager.total_score() == 0, "a fresh run scores nothing")

	# The daily board is frozen: a replay deals the very same scramble.
	var letters_before := ScrambledWordController.letters_to_text(ScrambledGameManager.controller.letters)
	ScrambledGameManager.mark_hint_used()
	var entry := ScrambledGameManager.solve_current_word()
	_check(int(entry.get("points", 0)) > 0, "a solved daily word scores")
	_check(ScrambledGameManager.total_score() == int(entry.get("points", 0)), "the total follows the word")
	_check(ScrambledGameManager.total_score() == ScrambledScoreManager.points_for(
		float(entry["seconds"]), true), "the recorded points come from the score table")

	ScrambledGameManager.reset()
	_check(ScrambledGameManager.start_competition(), "the daily run can be replayed")
	_check(ScrambledWordController.letters_to_text(ScrambledGameManager.controller.letters) == letters_before,
		"the daily scramble is identical on a replay")

	# A daily competition is limited to one attempt. Complete that attempt
	# before checking the score and attempt record.
	ScrambledGameManager.mark_hint_used()
	var guard := 0
	while ScrambledGameManager.state != ScrambledGameManager.State.FINISHED and guard < 50:
		ScrambledGameManager.solve_current_word()
		ScrambledGameManager.advance()
		guard += 1
	_check(ScrambledGameManager.state == ScrambledGameManager.State.FINISHED,
		"the daily run finishes")
	_check(ScrambledGameManager.correct_count() == ScrambledDailyPicker.WORDS_PER_DAY,
		"all five words were spelled (%d)" % ScrambledGameManager.correct_count())
	_check(ScrambledScoreManager.today_attempts() == 1,
		"the completed run is counted as one attempt")
	_check(ScrambledScoreManager.today_score() == ScrambledGameManager.total_score(),
		"the completed run owns the day's best (%d)" % ScrambledScoreManager.today_score())

	# Test abandoning in an isolated fresh record: it consumes its one daily
	# attempt and preserves the points earned before quitting.
	_remove_save()
	ScrambledScoreManager.reset_cache()
	ScrambledGameManager.reset()
	_check(ScrambledGameManager.start_competition(), "a fresh record allows a daily run")
	ScrambledGameManager.mark_hint_used()
	ScrambledGameManager.solve_current_word()
	ScrambledGameManager.abandon()
	_check(ScrambledScoreManager.today_played(), "a quit daily run still records its score")
	_check(ScrambledScoreManager.today_score() > 0, "the partial score is kept")
	_check(ScrambledScoreManager.today_attempts() == 1, "abandoning counts as one attempt")

	_remove_save()
	ScrambledScoreManager.reset_cache()
	ScrambledGameManager.reset()
	_check(ScrambledGameManager.start_competition(), "a fresh daily run can start before any words are solved")
	ScrambledGameManager.abandon()
	_check(ScrambledScoreManager.today_played(), "leaving before a solved word still locks the daily run")
	_check(ScrambledScoreManager.today_score() == 0, "an immediate exit records the current zero score")


############################################################
# BOARD (the drag-and-drop itself)
############################################################
## The pure modules above never touch the screen, so the drag pipeline is
## exercised here against a real board, driven from the board's side of the
## seam the native drag uses: the pickup is reported, the finger is followed,
## and the drop is delivered. The tile's own half of the protocol (the payload
## and the carried preview) is covered by test_tile_drag_payload.
func test_board_drag() -> void:
	var board_scene: PackedScene = load("res://scenes/word_game/scrambled/TileBoard.tscn")
	var board := board_scene.instantiate() as ScrambledTileBoard
	# The board's scene ships stretched, so a size set on it would be re-imposed
	# by the next layout pass: pin it to a fixed rect first.
	board.set_anchors_preset(Control.PRESET_TOP_LEFT)
	board.size = Vector2(1000, 420)
	add_child(board)
	await get_tree().process_frame
	await get_tree().process_frame

	var controller := ScrambledWordController.new()
	controller.setup({"word": "sun"}, 12345)
	var settled: Array = []
	board.arrangement_settled.connect(func(solved: bool) -> void: settled.append(solved))
	board.build(controller, false)
	await get_tree().process_frame

	_check(board.tile_count() == 3, "the board dealt three tiles")
	_check(ScrambledWordController.letters_to_text(board.tiles_letters())
		== ScrambledWordController.letters_to_text(controller.letters),
		"the board shows the scrambled letters (%s)" % board.current_text())
	_check(not board.is_solved(), "the dealt board is not solved")

	var first_tile: ScrambledTile = board.get_child(0)
	var second_tile: ScrambledTile = board.get_child(1)
	_check(first_tile.letter != "", "tiles carry letters")

	# Drag the first letter two slots to the right and drop it there, played
	# through the tile's own protocol exactly as the Viewport plays it.
	var drop_x := first_tile.position.x + first_tile.size.x * 0.5 + 700.0
	var payload: Variant = _begin_drag(first_tile)
	_check(first_tile.state == ScrambledTile.State.DRAGGING, "a picked-up letter is dragged")
	_check(board.is_busy(), "the board knows a letter is carried")

	_hover_drag(first_tile, payload, _board_point(board, drop_x, first_tile.position.y))
	_check(board._preview_index == 2, "dragging right opens the third slot")
	_end_drag(first_tile, payload, _board_point(board, drop_x, first_tile.position.y))
	await get_tree().create_timer(0.5).timeout
	_check(settled.size() >= 1 and not bool(settled[settled.size() - 1]),
		"the drop settled without solving")
	_check(first_tile.position.x > second_tile.position.x,
		"the carried tile landed in the slot it was dropped in")

	# Two more moves finish the word. The tile references are captured before
	# each pickup: starting a drag calls move_to_front(), which reorders the
	# children, so a fresh get_child(0) would name a different tile.
	for _move in 2:
		var dragged: ScrambledTile = board.get_child(0)
		_play_drag(board, dragged, dragged.position.x + dragged.size.x * 0.5 + 700.0)
		await get_tree().create_timer(0.5).timeout
	_check(bool(settled[settled.size() - 1]) == board.is_solved(),
		"the settle signal agrees with the board")
	_check(board.is_solved(), "the arranged board is solved (%s)" % board.current_text())
	_check(not board.is_busy(), "nothing is carried after a settle")

	board.queue_free()


## Regression: the first word of a session is dealt in the same frame the
## screen lays out, so the board is built before it knows its size, and the
## real layout only arrives a frame later — in the middle of the deal. The row
## must end up visible and on its slots: the deal fades in from alpha 0, so a
## deal abandoned (rather than restarted) would leave the letters invisible,
## and one still aimed at the pre-layout row would land them off the track.
func test_board_first_word_layout() -> void:
	var board_scene: PackedScene = load("res://scenes/word_game/scrambled/TileBoard.tscn")
	var board: Control = board_scene.instantiate()
	add_child(board)
	# Deliberately without a size: exactly the first frame of a session.
	var controller := ScrambledWordController.new()
	controller.setup({"word": "sun"}, 777)
	board.build(controller, true)
	await get_tree().process_frame
	_check(board.tile_count() == 3, "the first word is dealt before the board is sized")

	# The layout lands mid-deal: the deal is restarted against the real row.
	board.size = Vector2(1000, 420)
	_check(board._dealing, "a layout change mid-deal restarts the deal")
	await get_tree().create_timer(0.9).timeout

	var row_y := -1.0
	for i in board.tile_count():
		var tile: ScrambledTile = board.get_child(i)
		_check(is_equal_approx(tile.modulate.a, 1.0),
			"letter %d is visible after the deal (alpha %.2f)" % [i, tile.modulate.a])
		var slot: Vector2 = board._slot_position(i)
		_check(tile.position.distance_to(slot) < 2.0,
			"letter %d landed on its slot (%.0f,%.0f vs %.0f,%.0f)" % [i,
				tile.position.x, tile.position.y, slot.x, slot.y])
		_check(tile.position.y >= 0.0
			and tile.position.y + tile.size.y <= board.size.y + 1.0,
			"letter %d sits inside the board" % i)
		if row_y < 0.0:
			row_y = tile.position.y
			_check(true, "the dealt row has a baseline")
		else:
			_check(is_equal_approx(tile.position.y, row_y),
				"letter %d shares the row baseline" % i)
	board.queue_free()


## The same check on the real screen, containers and all: the gameplay screen
## builds the board and deals the first word inside its own _ready(), so the
## board is always built before it has been laid out. This is the path the
## player sees first, and the one that must never show an empty row.
func test_gameplay_first_word_visible() -> void:
	ScrambledScoreManager.reset_cache()
	ScrambledGameManager.reset()
	_check(ScrambledGameManager.start_learning(1, 2),
		"a learning session on Vision 1 / Lesson 2 starts")
	var screen_scene: PackedScene = load("res://scenes/word_game/scrambled/Gameplay.tscn")
	var screen: Control = screen_scene.instantiate()
	add_child(screen)
	await get_tree().create_timer(1.0).timeout

	var board: ScrambledTileBoard = screen._board
	_check(board != null, "the gameplay screen owns a board")
	if board == null:
		screen.queue_free()
		return
	_check(board.size.y > 100.0, "the board has a real size (%.0f)" % board.size.y)
	_check(board.tile_count() > 0,
		"the first word was dealt (%d letters)" % board.tile_count())
	var row_y := -1.0
	for i in board.tile_count():
		var tile := board.get_child(i) as ScrambledTile
		_check(tile != null, "child %d is a tile" % i)
		_check(tile.modulate.a > 0.99,
			"the first word's letter %d is visible (alpha %.2f)" % [i, tile.modulate.a])
		_check(tile.size.x > 32.0, "letter %d has a real size (%.0f)" % [i, tile.size.x])
		_check(tile.position.y >= 0.0
			and tile.position.y + tile.size.y <= board.size.y + 1.0,
			"letter %d sits inside the board (%.0f..%.0f of %.0f)" % [i,
				tile.position.y, tile.position.y + tile.size.y, board.size.y])
		if row_y < 0.0:
			row_y = tile.position.y
		else:
			_check(is_equal_approx(tile.position.y, row_y),
				"letter %d shares the row baseline" % i)
	screen.queue_free()
	ScrambledGameManager.abandon()


## The screen is laid out by containers, so every band has to land in its place
## in the column: nothing may overlap the band below it, the board must get the
## room the others leave, and the overlays must float over the lot. This is the
## guarantee splitting the screen into component scenes is for.
func test_gameplay_layout() -> void:
	ScrambledScoreManager.reset_cache()
	ScrambledGameManager.reset()
	_check(ScrambledGameManager.start_learning(1, 2), "a lesson starts for the layout check")
	var screen_scene: PackedScene = load("res://scenes/word_game/scrambled/Gameplay.tscn")
	var screen: Control = screen_scene.instantiate()
	add_child(screen)
	await get_tree().process_frame
	await get_tree().process_frame

	var band: Control = screen.get_node("Layout/MessageBand")
	var column: Array = [
		["the chips sit at the top of the column", screen._chips],
		["the clock sits under the chips", screen._timer],
		["the message band sits under the clock", band],
		["the board takes the room the rest leave", screen._board],
		["the action row closes the column", screen._actions],
	]
	var previous_bottom := 0.0
	for entry in column:
		var control: Control = entry[1]
		_check(control.size.y > 0.0, "%s (height %.0f)" % [entry[0], control.size.y])
		_check(control.position.y >= previous_bottom - 0.5,
			"%s: does not overlap what is above it (top %.0f after %.0f)"
			% [entry[0], control.position.y, previous_bottom])
		previous_bottom = control.position.y + control.size.y
	_check(previous_bottom <= screen.size.y + 1.0,
		"the column fits the screen (bottom %.0f of %.0f)" % [previous_bottom, screen.size.y])
	_check(screen._board.size.y >= 400.0,
		"the board clears its own minimum (%.0f)" % screen._board.size.y)
	_check(screen._hint_card.size.y > 0.0,
		"the meaning card is laid out inside the band (%.0f)" % screen._hint_card.size.y)

	# The feedback layers float above the column, so they must span the screen
	# rather than be pushed around by it.
	_check(is_equal_approx(screen._praise.size.x, screen.size.x)
		and is_equal_approx(screen._praise.size.y, screen.size.y),
		"the praise overlay covers the screen")
	_check(is_equal_approx(screen._confirm.size.x, screen.size.x)
		and is_equal_approx(screen._confirm.size.y, screen.size.y),
		"the quit question covers the screen")
	_check(not screen._confirm.is_open(), "the quit question stays shut until it is asked")

	screen.queue_free()
	ScrambledGameManager.abandon()


## The screen's looks come from a Theme now, so the THEME is what this test
## checks: each component is asked for a value only its variation could supply.
## A variation that stopped resolving would quietly fall back to the plain app
## look, and this is where that gets caught instead of by eye.
func test_gameplay_theme_variations() -> void:
	ScrambledScoreManager.reset_cache()
	ScrambledGameManager.reset()
	_check(ScrambledGameManager.start_learning(1, 2), "a lesson starts for the theme check")
	var screen_scene: PackedScene = load("res://scenes/word_game/scrambled/Gameplay.tscn")
	var screen: Control = screen_scene.instantiate()
	add_child(screen)
	await get_tree().process_frame
	await get_tree().process_frame

	_check(screen.theme != null, "the screen puts a theme in place")
	_check(screen.theme.default_font != null
		and screen.theme.default_font.resource_path == MenuStyle.FONT_VAZIR,
		"the game's theme carries the app's type face")
	_check(screen.theme.get_color("font_color", "Label") == MenuStyle.text(),
		"a plain label on this screen takes the app's text colour")

	# The chips: a pill's shape and its own accent can only come from the
	# variation, so a resolved rounded stylebox proves the wiring end to end.
	var progress := screen._chips.get_node("Progress") as Label
	var mode := screen._chips.get_node("Mode") as Label
	_check(progress.theme_type_variation == ScrambledTheme.V_CHIP_PROGRESS,
		"the progress chip names its variation")
	_check(progress.get_theme_stylebox("normal") is StyleBoxFlat,
		"the progress chip takes its pill shape from the theme")
	_check(progress.get_theme_font_size("font_size") > 0,
		"the progress chip takes its size from the theme (%.0f)"
			% progress.get_theme_font_size("font_size"))
	_check(mode.get_theme_color("font_color") != progress.get_theme_color("font_color"),
		"each chip keeps its own accent")

	# The clock: shape from the theme, colour from the clock itself.
	var bar := screen._timer.get_node("Bar") as ProgressBar
	_check(bar.theme_type_variation == ScrambledTheme.V_TIMER_BAR,
		"the clock bar names its variation")
	var fill := bar.get_theme_stylebox("fill")
	_check(fill is StyleBoxFlat and (fill as StyleBoxFlat).corner_radius_top_left > 0,
		"the clock's fill is a rounded block from the theme")

	# The buttons: the game's own candy look rather than the app's button.
	var hint := screen._actions.get_node("Hint") as Button
	_check(hint.theme_type_variation == ScrambledTheme.V_CANDY_BUTTON,
		"the hint button names the game's candy variation")
	_check(hint.get_theme_stylebox("normal") is StyleBoxFlat,
		"the hint button is painted by the theme")

	# The two answers: one variation each, so the pair reads as one choice.
	var stay := screen._confirm.get_node("Center/Card/Margin/Column/Choices/Stay") as Button
	_check(stay.theme_type_variation == ScrambledTheme.V_SAFE_BUTTON,
		"the dialog's safe answer names its variation")
	_check(stay.get_theme_stylebox("normal") is StyleBoxFlat,
		"the dialog's safe answer is painted by the theme")
	_check(stay.get_theme_font_size("font_size") == ScrambledTheme.DIALOG_BUTTON_FONT_SIZE,
		"the dialog's answers share one size (%.0f)" % stay.get_theme_font_size("font_size"))

	# The how-to line and the meaning card.
	_check(screen._instruction.get_theme_font_size("font_size") > 0,
		"the how-to line takes its size from the theme")
	_check(screen._hint_card.get_theme_stylebox("panel") is StyleBoxFlat,
		"the meaning card's paper comes from the theme")

	screen.queue_free()
	ScrambledGameManager.abandon()


## The payload and the carried preview are the only contract between a drag and
## a drop target, so the tile's half of the protocol is checked on its own —
## including the payload shapes that must be refused.
func test_tile_drag_payload() -> void:
	var board: ScrambledTileBoard = await _make_board("sun", 4242)

	var tile: ScrambledTile = board.get_child(0)
	# A locked letter (the beat between two words) must not start a drag at all.
	tile.set_locked(true)
	_check(tile._get_drag_data(Vector2.ZERO) == null, "a locked letter refuses to be dragged")
	tile.set_locked(false)

	var payload: Variant = tile._get_drag_data(Vector2.ZERO)
	# The carried copy belongs to the engine, so it is only handed over during a
	# real drag: asking outside one has to stay silent rather than trip the
	# engine's guard.
	_check(tile.get_viewport().gui_get_drag_data() == null,
		"no preview is handed to a drag that is not running")
	_check(typeof(payload) == TYPE_DICTIONARY, "a draggable letter hands over a payload")
	_check(ScrambledTile.payload_tile(payload) == tile, "the payload names its own letter")
	_check(tile.state == ScrambledTile.State.DRAGGING, "the letter knows it is being dragged")
	_check(ScrambledTile.payload_tile({"kind": "some_other_screen"}) == null,
		"a payload from another screen is refused")
	_check(ScrambledTile.payload_tile("not a payload") == null,
		"a payload that is not a dictionary is refused")

	# The engine ends every drag with this notification. Nothing took this
	# letter, so the board must be told and the carried ghost must fade back;
	# the row then settles and hands the letters back, ready to be picked up.
	tile._notification(Control.NOTIFICATION_DRAG_END)
	_check(not board.is_busy(), "the board stops carrying the letter")
	await get_tree().create_timer(0.5).timeout
	_check(tile.state == ScrambledTile.State.IDLE, "the letter is playable again once the row settles")
	_check(is_equal_approx(tile.modulate.a, 1.0),
		"the carried ghost fades back to solid (alpha %.2f)" % tile.modulate.a)

	board.queue_free()


############################################################
# HELPERS
############################################################
func _word_list(entries: Array) -> Array:
	var out: Array = []
	for entry in entries:
		out.append(str((entry as Dictionary).get("word", "")))
	return out


## A drag that ends anywhere but over the row must put the letter back exactly
## where it came from: a slipped finger can never scramble the word for free,
## and a letter can never be lost off the row.
func test_board_drag_cancel() -> void:
	var board: ScrambledTileBoard = await _make_board("sun", 20250924)
	var before := board.current_text()
	var carried: ScrambledTile = board.get_child(0)

	# The finger travels two slots right — the slot really does open — and then
	# lifts somewhere the row does not accept.
	var payload: Variant = _begin_drag(carried)
	_hover_drag(carried, payload,
		_board_point(board, carried.position.x + 700.0, carried.position.y))
	_check(board._preview_index == 2, "the cancellation case really did open a slot")
	carried._notification(Control.NOTIFICATION_DRAG_END)
	await get_tree().create_timer(0.5).timeout

	_check(not board.is_busy(), "nothing is carried after a cancelled drag")
	_check(board.current_text() == before,
		"a cancelled drag leaves the word alone (%s)" % board.current_text())
	_check(is_equal_approx(carried.modulate.a, 1.0), "the cancelled letter is solid again")

	board.queue_free()


func _check(condition: bool, label: String) -> void:
	if not condition:
		_failures += 1
	print(("PASS  " if condition else "FAIL  ") + label)


## A real, laid-out board with one word dealt — the fixture the drag tests
## need. The board guesses its geometry when it is built before it has been
## laid out, so the fixture waits for the real size twice, exactly as the live
## screen does on the frame it appears.
func _make_board(word: String, seed_value: int) -> ScrambledTileBoard:
	var controller := ScrambledWordController.new()
	controller.setup({"word": word}, seed_value)
	var board_scene: PackedScene = load("res://scenes/word_game/scrambled/TileBoard.tscn")
	var board := board_scene.instantiate() as ScrambledTileBoard
	# The board's scene ships stretched, so a size set on it would be re-imposed
	# by the next layout pass: pin it to a fixed rect first.
	board.set_anchors_preset(Control.PRESET_TOP_LEFT)
	board.size = Vector2(1000, 420)
	add_child(board)
	await get_tree().process_frame
	await get_tree().process_frame
	board.build(controller, false)
	await get_tree().process_frame
	return board


## Plays one whole gesture exactly as the Viewport plays it: the tile is asked
## for its payload (which is when it builds the preview the player carries),
## the finger is followed, and the letter is let go at `drop_x`.
func _play_drag(board: ScrambledTileBoard, tile: ScrambledTile, drop_x: float) -> void:
	var payload: Variant = _begin_drag(tile)
	_hover_drag(tile, payload, _board_point(board, drop_x, tile.position.y))
	_end_drag(tile, payload, _board_point(board, drop_x, tile.position.y))


## The Viewport's drag start: the tile hands over its payload, and its own
## drag_started signal is what tells the board to open a slot.
func _begin_drag(tile: ScrambledTile) -> Variant:
	return tile._get_drag_data(Vector2.ZERO)


## The Viewport asking whatever is under the finger whether it would take the
## letter — the letter is hovered over the row, so the row itself answers.
func _hover_drag(tile: ScrambledTile, payload: Variant, canvas_point: Vector2) -> bool:
	var local := tile.get_global_transform().affine_inverse() * canvas_point
	return tile._can_drop_data(local, payload)


## The finger lifting over the row: the drop is delivered and the engine's
## end-of-drag notification follows, exactly as in a live drag.
func _end_drag(tile: ScrambledTile, payload: Variant, canvas_point: Vector2) -> void:
	var local := tile.get_global_transform().affine_inverse() * canvas_point
	tile._drop_data(local, payload)
	tile._notification(Control.NOTIFICATION_DRAG_END)


## A finger position over the row, in the shared canvas space the drag protocol
## speaks (the board reaches its own space through _to_board).
func _board_point(board: ScrambledTileBoard, x: float, y: float) -> Vector2:
	return board.get_global_transform() * Vector2(x, y)
```

## File: `res://tests/test_srs_leitner.gd`

```gdscript
extends Node
## ============================================================
##  SPACED REPETITION / LEITNER TESTS
##
##  Covers the scheduler maths, the saved-words + review-words save
##  system, and the queue semantics the WordReview scene relies on.
##
##  These tests call Global.save_word()/remove_word(), which write to user://.
##  The test runner invokes every test_* method INDIVIDUALLY in addition to
##  running them from _ready, so protecting the files in _ready alone is not
##  enough — each test that touches disk has to wrap itself in _protect(),
##  which snapshots both save files and restores them afterwards.
## ============================================================

const SAVED_PATH   := "user://saved_words.json"
const REVIEW_PATH  := "user://review_words.json"

var _failures := 0
var _parked := {}


func _ready() -> void:
	_park_user_files()

	test_interval_ordering()
	test_hard_never_outlasts_good()
	test_interval_is_capped()
	test_again_stays_due_today()
	test_preview_matches_schedule()
	test_preview_does_not_mutate()
	test_corrupt_fields_are_normalised()
	test_sanitize_drops_junk_and_duplicates()
	test_save_word_is_idempotent()
	test_save_seeds_srs_fields()
	test_remove_is_a_noop_when_absent()
	test_remove_saved_word_keeps_review_card()
	test_remove_review_word_keeps_saved_word()
	test_resaving_restores_missing_review_card()
	test_review_word_reschedules_in_both_lists()
	test_due_words_returns_copies()
	test_due_words_sorts_most_overdue_first()
	test_due_words_caps_new_cards()
	test_corrupt_save_file_loads_empty()

	_restore_user_files()

	print("---")
	print("ALL TESTS PASSED" if _failures == 0 else "%d TEST(S) FAILED" % _failures)


############################################################
# SCHEDULER MATHS
############################################################

## The four ratings must never disagree about which is sooner: picking a
## harsher answer has to bring the card back at least as early.
func test_interval_ordering() -> void:
	for reps in [0, 1, 2, 5, 12]:
		var entry := _entry(0.0, 2.5, reps)
		var again: Dictionary = Global._compute_srs_result(entry, "again")
		var hard: Dictionary  = Global._compute_srs_result(entry, "hard")
		var good: Dictionary  = Global._compute_srs_result(entry, "good")
		var easy: Dictionary  = Global._compute_srs_result(entry, "easy")

		print("reps=%d  again=%d hard=%d good=%d easy=%d" % [
			reps, again["due"], hard["due"], good["due"], easy["due"]
		])
		_check(again["due"] <= hard["due"], "again must not be later than hard (reps=%d)" % reps)
		_check(hard["due"] <= good["due"], "hard must not be later than good (reps=%d)" % reps)
		_check(good["due"] <= easy["due"], "good must not be later than easy (reps=%d)" % reps)


## Regression: a brand new card rated "hard" used to compute 1.2 days, which
## ceil() turned into +2 days, pushing it FURTHER away than "good" (+1 day).
func test_hard_never_outlasts_good() -> void:
	var fresh := _entry(0.0, 2.5, 0)
	var hard := Global._compute_srs_result(fresh, "hard")
	var good := Global._compute_srs_result(fresh, "good")
	var easy := Global._compute_srs_result(fresh, "easy")
	print("new card: hard=+%d(%s) good=+%d(%s) easy=+%d(%s)" % [
		hard["due"], Global._format_interval(hard["interval"], "hard"),
		good["due"], Global._format_interval(good["interval"], "good"),
		easy["due"], Global._format_interval(easy["interval"], "easy"),
	])
	_check(hard["due"] <= good["due"], "hard on a new card must not outlast good")
	# The three choices must be visibly distinct on the very first card, or
	# the student sees the same "۱ روز" on two buttons and cannot choose.
	_check(hard["due"] < good["due"], "hard must be sooner than good on a new card")
	_check(good["due"] < easy["due"], "good must be sooner than easy on a new card")
	_check(Global._format_interval(hard["interval"], "hard") == "امروز",
		"a sub-day hard interval must read as today, not '۱ روز'")
	_check(Global._format_interval(good["interval"], "good") == "۱ روز",
		"good on a new card should read as one day")
	_check(Global._format_interval(easy["interval"], "easy") != "۱ روز",
		"easy on a new card must not also read as one day")


func test_interval_is_capped() -> void:
	var wild := _entry(200.0, 3.0, 9)
	var r := Global._compute_srs_result(wild, "easy")
	print("capped interval=", r["interval"])
	_check(r["interval"] <= Global.SRS_MAX_INTERVAL, "interval exceeded SRS_MAX_INTERVAL")


## "again" is re-queued inside the same session, so it must stay due today.

## The label shown on the button is derived from the same interval that

## preview_intervals() is called on every "Show answer" tap. It used to call

func test_sanitize_drops_junk_and_duplicates() -> void:
```
